children.translated_text: <s>Caitanyam ātmā</s> (Consciousness is the self) // SivS 1.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śivasūtra</s>, First <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Awakening)

children.text: * caitanyaṃ citkriyārūpaṃ śivasya paramasya yat || SivSV_1.1:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness), whose nature is the knowledge and action (<s>cit-kriyā</s>) of the supreme <s>Śiva</s>, || SivSV 1.1:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * svātantryam etad evātmā tato 'sau paramaḥ śivaḥ || SivSV_1.1:2 ||
body.translated_text: That very freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) is the <s>Ātman</s> (self); therefore he is the supreme <s>Śiva</s>. || SivSV 1.1:2 ||

body.text: * athavā ko 'yam ātmeti praṣṭ bodhayituṃ śiśūn || SivSV_1.1:3 ||
body.translated_text: Or, to answer the question 'who is this <s>Ātman</s>?' and to instruct the students: || SivSV 1.1:3 ||

body.text: * nātmā deho na ca prāṇo na manaḥ khaṃ na śūnyabhūḥ || SivSV_1.1:4 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Ātman</s> is not the body, not <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), not the mind, not space, not the void; || SivSV 1.1:4 ||

body.text: * kiṃtu caitanyam evātmety ādiṣṭaṃ parameṣṭhinā || SivSV_1.1:5 ||
body.translated_text: But <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) alone is the <s>Ātman</s> — thus it is taught by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme Lord). || SivSV 1.1:5 ||

body.text: * atha caitanyam evaitad ātmā svābhāvikaṃ vapuḥ || SivSV_1.1:6 ||
body.translated_text: Now, <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness) itself is the <s>Ātman</s>, its natural body; || SivSV 1.1:6 ||

body.text: * viśeṣācodanād asya jagataś cety arūpiṇaḥ || SivSV_1.1:7 ||
body.translated_text: Because there is no specific instruction [distinguishing it] from the formless world. || SivSV 1.1:7 ||

body.text: * acetyamānaṃ kasyāpi vapuḥ kim api no bhavet || SivSV_1.1:8 ||
body.translated_text: That which is not cognized by anyone — could such a body exist at all? || SivSV 1.1:8 ||

body.text: * cetyamānaṃ tu cidrūpatādātmyāc cinmayaṃ bhavet || SivSV_1.1:9 ||
body.translated_text: But that which is cognized, being identical with the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>), becomes consciousness itself. || SivSV 1.1:9 ||
Thus, by the method taught by <s>Śiva</s>, of all beings — moving and stationary — || SivSV 1.1:10 ||

body.text: * caitanyam eva viśvasya svarūpaṃ pāramārthikam || SivSV_1.1:11 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Caitanya</s> (consciousness) alone is the true essential nature of the universe. || SivSV 1.1:11 ||

body.text: * nanv evaṃvidhaviśvasya caitanyaṃ ced vapus tadā || SivSV_1.1:12 ||
body.translated_text: But if consciousness is indeed the body of such a universe, || SivSV 1.1:12 ||

body.text: * kathaṃ bandhasya sambandha iti śaṅkāṃ vyapohitum || SivSV_1.1:13 ||
body.translated_text: Then how is there any connection with bondage? To remove this doubt, || SivSV 1.1:13 ||
The great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) states the [next] <s>sūtra</s> with both the joined and separated readings. || SivSV 1.1:14 ||
<s>Jñānaṃ bandhaḥ</s> (Knowledge is bondage) // SivS 1.2 //

children.translated_text: Ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>) is the first [type]: in the self whose nature is the expansion of consciousness, || SivSV 1.2:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * ātmany anātmatājñānaṃ jñānaṃ punar anātmani || SivSV_1.2:2 ||
body.translated_text: The false cognition of non-self in the self; and knowledge [in the second sense] is || SivSV 1.2:2 ||

body.text: * dehādāv ātmamānitvaṃ dvayam apy etad āṇavam || SivSV_1.2:3 ||
body.translated_text: The false attribution of selfhood to the non-self such as the body, etc. — both of these constitute the <s>āṇava</s> || SivSV 1.2:3 ||

body.text: * malaṃ svakalpitaṃ svasmin bandhaḥ svecchāvibhāvitaḥ || SivSV_1.2:4 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Mala</s> (impurity), self-imagined upon oneself; bondage is manifested by one's own will. || SivSV 1.2:4 ||

body.text: * kim āṇavamalātmaiva bandho 'yaṃ nety udīryate || SivSV_1.2:5 ||]
body.translated_text: Is this bondage constituted solely of <s>āṇavamala</s>? No — [it is further] stated: || SivSV 1.2:5 ||
<s>Yonivargaḥ kalāśarīram</s> (The source-group is the body of <s>kalā</s>) // SivS 1.3 //

children.text: * yonir bhedaprathāhetur māyā vargas tadutthitaḥ || SivSV_1.3:1 ||
children.translated_text: The <s>yoni</s> (source) is <s>Māyā</s>, the cause of the manifestation of differentiation; the <s>varga</s> (group) arises from it; || SivSV 1.3:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The collection of <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from <s>Kalā</s> to earth — that has its nature. || SivSV 1.3:2 ||
The <s>māyīya mala</s> (impurity of Māyā), consisting of the manifestation of differentiated objects of knowledge, || SivSV 1.3:3 ||

body.text: * kaleti kāyam āviśya paricchedakarī nṛṇām || SivSV_1.3:4 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Kalā</s>, entering the body, creates limitation in beings; || SivSV 1.3:4 ||

body.text: * vyāpṛtiḥ puṇyapāpātmā śarīraṃ yasya tat punaḥ || SivSV_1.3:5 ||
body.translated_text: Activity in the form of merit and sin — that is the body [of <s>kārma mala</s>]; || SivSV 1.3:5 ||

body.text: * kārmaṃ ca malam etasmin dvaye bandho 'nuvartate || SivSV_1.3:6 ||
body.translated_text: And the <s>kārma mala</s> (impurity of action) — in these two [māyīya and kārma], bondage continues. || SivSV 1.3:6 ||
In the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition of the Lord), this triad of <s>malas</s> (impurities) has been stated: || SivSV 1.3:7 ||
Loss of freedom of awareness, and lack of awareness of [one's] freedom — || SivSV 1.3:8 ||
This <s>āṇavamala</s> is twofold, through the removal of one's true nature; || SivSV 1.3:9 ||
In the manifestation of differentiated objects alone, <s>māyīyamala</s> grants birth and experience; || SivSV 1.3:10 ||

body.text: * kartary abodhe kārmaṃ tu māyāśaktyaiva tat trayam || SivSV_1.3:11 ||
body.translated_text: When the agent lacks awareness, [there arises] <s>kārmamala</s> — but all three [operate] through <s>Māyā-śakti</s> alone. || SivSV 1.3:11 ||

body.text: * ity athaiṣāṃ malānāṃ tu bandhakatvaṃ nirūpyate || SivSV_1.3:12 ||]
body.translated_text: Thus, the binding nature of these <s>malas</s> (impurities) is now being established. || SivSV 1.3:12 ||
<s>Jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkā</s> (The basis of knowledge is <s>Mātṛkā</s>) // SivS 1.4 //

children.translated_text: Incomplete, having the nature of otherness, consisting of the manifestation of differentiated objects, || SivSV 1.4:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Having the form of all the impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) of actions both auspicious and inauspicious, || SivSV 1.4:2 ||

body.text: * trividhaṃ malam uktaṃ yat tad eva jñānam ucyate || SivSV_1.4:3 ||
body.translated_text: The threefold <s>mala</s> (impurity) that has been stated — that itself is called 'knowledge' [here]. || SivSV 1.4:3 ||

body.text: * na so 'sti pratyayo loke yaḥ śabdānugamād ṛte || SivSV_1.4:4 ||
body.translated_text: There is no cognition in the world that exists without the accompaniment of words; || SivSV 1.4:4 ||

body.text: * anuviddham iva jñānaṃ sarvaṃ śabdena gamyate || SivSV_1.4:5 ||
body.translated_text: All knowledge is understood as if pervaded by words. || SivSV 1.4:5 ||

body.text: * ity uktanītyā jñānasya vividhasyāsya mātṛkā || SivSV_1.4:6 ||
body.translated_text: By the stated principle, the <s>Mātṛkā</s> (Mother of letters) is the basis of this manifold knowledge, || SivSV 1.4:6 ||
Embodied as the fifty letters from 'a' to 'kṣa', || SivSV 1.4:7 ||
The source of the entire collection of <s>tattvas</s> from <s>Śiva</s> to earth. || SivSV 1.4:8 ||
Stationed within the openings of consciousness, supporting the nooses of <s>Brahmā</s>, || SivSV 1.4:9 ||
The <s>Pīṭheśvarīs</s> (Goddesses of the sacred seats), greatly terrible, delude again and again. || SivSV 1.4:10 ||
Thus, following the method taught in the sacred <s>Timirodghāṭa</s> (Dispelling of Darkness), || SivSV 1.4:11 ||
Adorned by the circle of <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers) presiding over the vowels and consonant groups, || SivSV 1.4:12 ||

body.text: * apūrṇo 'ham ahaṃ pūrṇo 'haṃ kṛśo 'haṃ kṛśetaraḥ || SivSV_1.4:13 ||
body.translated_text: 'I am incomplete,' 'I am complete,' 'I am thin,' 'I am not thin' — || SivSV 1.4:13 ||
Thus, through the pervasion of words, [the Mātṛkā] causes grief, joy, and the like. || SivSV 1.4:14 ||
As the foundation, as the presiding [power] — through its governance of beings, || SivSV 1.4:15 ||
Not having attained the repose of the inward-turned self, constantly || SivSV 1.4:16 ||
Outward-directed cognitions are said to be the causes of bondage. || SivSV 1.4:17 ||
Now the means for the pacification of such bondage-connection is stated — || SivSV 1.4:18 ||
Having the true nature of repose in the supreme goal, by <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (the Supreme Lord): || SivSV 1.4:19 ||
<s>Udyamo bhairavaḥ</s> (The upsurge is <s>Bhairava</s>) // SivS 1.5 //

children.translated_text: That which, of the self-awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) whose nature is reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>), as it expands, || SivSV 1.5:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Has the nature of the sudden emergence of an intuitive flash (<s>pratibhā</s>) in the form of instantaneous upsurge, || SivSV 1.5:2 ||
That upsurge (<s>udyama</s>) is the inner vibration (<s>spanda</s>), having the nature of the full 'I'-consciousness (<s>pūrṇāhambhāvanā</s>). || SivSV 1.5:3 ||

body.text: * sa eva sarvaśaktīnāṃ sāmarasyād aśeṣataḥ || SivSV_1.5:4 ||
body.translated_text: That alone, through the equipoise of all powers, completely, || SivSV 1.5:4 ||
Through being filled from all sides, of the differentiating <s>vikalpas</s> (conceptual constructs), || SivSV 1.5:5 ||

body.text: * alaṃ kavalanenāpīty anvarthād eva bhairavaḥ || SivSV_1.5:6 ||
body.translated_text: Being capable of swallowing [them all] — thus by the very meaning [of the word], [it is called] <s>Bhairava</s>. || SivSV 1.5:6 ||
Now, from such attainment of the <s>Bhairava</s> [state], which causes the pacification of bondage, || SivSV 1.5:7 ||

body.text: * vyutthānaṃ ca bhavec chāntabhedābhāsam itīryate || SivSV_1.5:8 ||]
body.translated_text: Even the emergence [from absorption] becomes free from the appearance of differentiation — thus it is stated. || SivSV 1.5:8 ||
<s>Śakti-cakra-saṃdhāne viśva-saṃhāraḥ</s> (In the union with the wheel of powers, dissolution of the universe) // SivS 1.6 //

children.text: * yo 'yam uktaḥ svasaṃvitter udyamo bhairavātmakaḥ || SivSV_1.6:1 ||
children.translated_text: This upsurge of self-awareness that has been described as having the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>, || SivSV 1.6:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
It has a great power that transcends both sequence and non-sequence; || SivSV 1.6:2 ||
Eager to pervade the entire wheel of one's own powers of consciousness, || SivSV 1.6:3 ||
Empty, non-empty, both, or having none of these forms — it is the supreme [power]. || SivSV 1.6:4 ||
By which, upon the wall of one's own consciousness, beginning from the manifestation of the object of knowledge, || SivSV 1.6:5 ||
Having the form of vibration (<s>spanda</s>) culminating in the repose of the supreme knowing subject, || SivSV 1.6:6 ||
Through the expansion of the powers of manifestation called creation, maintenance, and dissolution, || SivSV 1.6:7 ||
The fivefold activity (<s>pañcakṛtya</s>) extending to the realm of manifestation is displayed. || SivSV 1.6:8 ||

body.text: * tayā prasāritasyāsya śakticakrasya yat punaḥ || SivSV_1.6:9 ||
body.translated_text: Of this wheel of powers, expanded by that [upsurge], the || SivSV 1.6:9 ||
Union (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) is the reflective awareness of the order revealed in the inner tradition; || SivSV 1.6:10 ||

body.text: * tasmin saty asya viśvasya kālāgnyādikalāvadheḥ || SivSV_1.6:11 ||
body.translated_text: When that [union] occurs, of this universe extending up to the phase of <s>Kālāgni</s> (the fire of time), || SivSV 1.6:11 ||
There is dissolution, characterized by the establishment of the fire of one's own consciousness. || SivSV 1.6:12 ||
Thus, for the <s>yogī</s> whose differentiation has been consumed by the fire of his own consciousness, || SivSV 1.6:13 ||

body.text: * na syāt samādhivyutthānabhedaḥ ko 'pīti kathyate || SivSV_1.6:14 ||
body.translated_text: There would be no distinction between <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) and <s>vyutthāna</s> (emergence) — thus it is stated. || SivSV 1.6:14 ||
In the distinction between waking, dream, and deep sleep — the experience of the <s>Turya</s> (Fourth state) arises; || SivSV 1.6:15 ||

body.text: * udyamo bhairava iti proktarūpaṃ sphuradvapuḥ || SivSV_1.6:16 ||
body.translated_text: 'The upsurge is <s>Bhairava</s>' — the stated form, the vibrating body; || SivSV 1.6:16 ||

body.text: * turyaṃ nāma paraṃ dhāma tadābhogaś camatkriyā || SivSV_1.6:17 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Turya</s> by name, the supreme abode — its experience is <s>camatkāra</s> (wonder). || SivSV 1.6:17 ||

body.text: * bhede 'pi jāgradādīnāṃ yoginas tasya sambhavaḥ || SivSV_1.6:18 ||
body.translated_text: Even in the differentiation of waking and the other [states], for that <s>yogī</s>, its arising — || SivSV 1.6:18 ||

body.text: * anusyūtiḥ parānandarūpā syād iti śiṣyate || SivSV_1.6:19 ||
body.translated_text: The pervasion whose form is supreme bliss — thus it is taught. || SivSV 1.6:19 ||
The triad of waking and the other [states] is characterized by a triad of <s>sūtras</s> in sequence: || SivSV 1.6:20 ||
<s>Jñānaṃ jāgrat</s> (Knowledge is waking) // SivS 1.7 //
<s>Svapno vikalpāḥ</s> (Dreams are thought-constructs) // SivS 1.8 //
<s>Aviveko māyā sauṣuptam</s> (Non-discrimination, which is <s>Māyā</s>, is deep sleep) // SivS 1.9 //

children.translated_text: Knowledge born of the external senses is waking — having objects common to all; || SivSV 1.9:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * svapnaḥ svātmaiva samprokto vikalpāḥ svātmasambhavāḥ || SivSV_1.9:2 ||
body.translated_text: Dream is said to be one's own self — <s>vikalpas</s> (thought-constructs) arise from one's own self; || SivSV 1.9:2 ||

body.text: * aviveko nijākhyātir māyā mohas tadātmakaḥ || SivSV_1.9:3 ||
body.translated_text: Non-discrimination is the non-recognition of one's own [nature]; <s>Māyā</s> is delusion, having that nature; || SivSV 1.9:3 ||

body.text: * sauṣuptaṃ yoginām etat tritayaṃ dhāraṇādikam || SivSV_1.9:4 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Sauṣupta</s> (deep sleep) — for <s>yogīs</s>, this triad [corresponds to] <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and the rest. || SivSV 1.9:4 ||
In the <s>Īśvarapratyabhijñā</s> (Recognition of the Lord), waking and the others are also characterized || SivSV 1.9:5 ||
In the void, having the nature of the absence of <s>buddhi</s> (intellect) and the rest, [with] the condition of I-ness and agency, || SivSV 1.9:6 ||
In which there are only faint, formless impressions — [there is] absence of objects of knowledge; || SivSV 1.9:7 ||

body.text: * sākṣāṇām āntarī vṛttiḥ prāṇādiprerikā matā || SivSV_1.9:8 ||
body.translated_text: The inner activity of the senses, regarded as the impeller of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, || SivSV 1.9:8 ||
Or the I-consciousness called 'life' (<s>jīvana</s>), in <s>prāṇa</s>, having the nature of the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body) — || SivSV 1.9:9 ||

body.text: * tāvan mātrasthitau proktaṃ sauṣuptaṃ pralayopamam || SivSV_1.9:10 ||
body.translated_text: Abiding in that mere [state of limited subjectivity], it is called <s>sauṣupta</s> (deep sleep), resembling dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>); || SivSV 1.9:10 ||
With objects and without objects, with and without <s>Māyā-mala</s> (impurity of Māyā). || SivSV 1.9:11 ||
Even in the path of the mind alone, through the delusion of [appearing as] objects of the senses, || SivSV 1.9:12 ||

body.text: * spaṣṭāvabhāsā bhāvānāṃ sṛṣṭiḥ svapnapadaṃ matam || SivSV_1.9:13 ||
body.translated_text: The clear manifestation of things — creation [in this mode] is regarded as the state of dream. || SivSV 1.9:13 ||

body.text: * sarvākṣagocaratvena yā tu bāhyatayā sthirā || SivSV_1.9:14 ||
body.translated_text: But that [creation] which, by being the object of all senses, is stable and external, || SivSV 1.9:14 ||

body.text: * sṛṣṭiḥ sādhāraṇī sarvapramātṇāṃ sa jāgaraḥ || SivSV_1.9:15 ||
body.translated_text: The creation common to all knowing subjects — that is waking. || SivSV 1.9:15 ||
Thus, having been described at length following worldly and yogic [perspectives], || SivSV 1.9:16 ||
In this triad of waking and the others, for one who is awake through attention, || SivSV 1.9:17 ||
Through union with the wheel of powers, which is the cause of the dissolution of the universe, || SivSV 1.9:18 ||
The recognition of non-difference pervaded by the experience of the <s>Turya</s> (Fourth state), which destroys non-recognition — || SivSV 1.9:19 ||

body.text: * sphuraty avirataṃ yasya sa taddhārādhirohataḥ || SivSV_1.9:20 ||
body.translated_text: That flashes forth unceasingly for one who, by ascending into the stream of that [Turya], || SivSV 1.9:20 ||
The <s>yogī</s>, pervaded by the <s>Turyātīta</s> (state beyond the Fourth), touches the stated <s>caitanya</s> (consciousness). || SivSV 1.9:21 ||
<s>Tritayabhoktā vīreśaḥ</s> (The enjoyer of the triad is the lord of heroes) // SivS 1.10 //

children.translated_text: The triad of waking and the others, through union with the stated wheel of powers, || SivSV 1.10:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Sprinkled with the essence of the bliss of <s>Turya</s>, through the abandonment of differentiation, || SivSV 1.10:2 ||
Contemplating the supreme space immersed in the nectar of bliss, || SivSV 1.10:3 ||

body.text: * tritayasyāsya yo bhoktā camatkartā sa yogirāṭ || SivSV_1.10:4 ||
body.translated_text: One who is the enjoyer of this triad, the one who marvels — that king of <s>yogīs</s>, || SivSV 1.10:4 ||

body.text: * triṣu dhāmasu yad bhogyaṃ bhoktā yaś ca prakīrtitaḥ || SivSV_1.10:5 ||
body.translated_text: In the three states, what is enjoyed and who is declared as the enjoyer — || SivSV 1.10:5 ||

body.text: * vidyāt tad ubhayaṃ yas tu sa bhuñjāno na lipyate || SivSV_1.10:6 ||
body.translated_text: One who knows both these — that one, while enjoying, is not tainted. || SivSV 1.10:6 ||
Thus, possessing the glory of the sovereignty of consciousness that has no rival, || SivSV 1.10:7 ||
A mass of consciousness, filled with the supreme bliss of self-knowledge, || SivSV 1.10:8 ||
He is <s>Vīreśa</s> (Lord of Heroes), because of the heroes (<s>vīras</s>) — [the senses] which devour differentiation, || SivSV 1.10:9 ||
Moving inward and outward — he is the sovereign lord of the senses. || SivSV 1.10:10 ||
Are there stages for him that indicate the repose of ascending to the supreme consciousness-principle? || SivSV 1.10:11 ||

body.text: * bhūmikāḥ santy ayaṃ yābhir yāti sarvottarāṃ sthitim || SivSV_1.10:12 ||
body.translated_text: The stages by which he attains the most supreme state — || SivSV 1.10:12 ||
To allay the doubt in the student's heart, 'they exist' — thus it is stated: || SivSV 1.10:13 ||
<s>Vismayo yogabhūmikāḥ</s> (Wonder is the stages of <s>yoga</s>) // SivS 1.11 //

children.text: * yathā sātiśayānande kasyacid vismayo bhavet || SivSV_1.11:1 ||
children.translated_text: Just as, in an experience of ever-increasing bliss, wonder arises for someone, || SivSV 1.11:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
So too for this <s>yogī</s>, constantly, in the perception of each and every object of knowledge, || SivSV 1.11:2 ||
In the experience of the supreme bliss beyond comparison, with senses stilled, || SivSV 1.11:3 ||

body.text: * pare svātmany atṛptyaiva yad āścaryaṃ sa vismayaḥ || SivSV_1.11:4 ||
body.translated_text: The wonder which is the insatiability with one's own supreme self — that is <s>vismaya</s> (wonder). || SivSV 1.11:4 ||

body.text: * sa eva khalu yogasya paratattvaikyarūpiṇaḥ || SivSV_1.11:5 ||
body.translated_text: That indeed is the stages of <s>yoga</s>, whose nature is unity with the supreme principle, || SivSV 1.11:5 ||
The stages that indicate the repose of the supreme [self] through sequential ascent. || SivSV 1.11:6 ||
For one whose mind has ascended to such stages of <s>yoga</s> characterized by wonder, || SivSV 1.11:7 ||
<s>Icchā śaktir umā kumārī</s> (The will-power is <s>Umā</s>, the maiden) // SivS 1.12 //

children.translated_text: For that very <s>yogī</s> who has through proper means attained the eternal state of the supreme <s>Bhairava</s>, || SivSV 1.12:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * tasyaiva yogino yecchā śaktiḥ saiva bhavaty umā || SivSV_1.12:2 ||
body.translated_text: His will (<s>icchā</s>) is the power (<s>śakti</s>); that itself becomes <s>Umā</s>; || SivSV 1.12:2 ||

body.text: * parā bhaṭṭārikā saiva kumārīti prakīrtitā || SivSV_1.12:3 ||
body.translated_text: The supreme <s>Bhaṭṭārikā</s> (Goddess), she is called <s>Kumārī</s> (the Maiden). || SivSV 1.12:3 ||
Through the play of creation, etc. of the universe from <s>Sadāśiva</s> to earth, || SivSV 1.12:4 ||

body.text: * kumārī kuṃ mahāmāyābhūmiṃ mārayatīty api || SivSV_1.12:5 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Kumārī</s> — because she destroys (<s>mārayati</s>) the domain (<s>ku</s>) of <s>Mahāmāyā</s> — [she is so called]. || SivSV 1.12:5 ||
And <s>Kumārī</s> is the object of experience for this <s>yogī</s> of the nature of <s>Bhairava</s>; || SivSV 1.12:6 ||

body.text: * kumārī nānyabhogyā ca bhoktraikātmyena tiṣṭhati || SivSV_1.12:7 ||
body.translated_text: And <s>Kumārī</s> is not for the enjoyment of another — she abides in oneness with the enjoyer. || SivSV 1.12:7 ||
<s>Umā</s> <s>Kumārī</s>, having abandoned all attachments, devoted to the worship of <s>Maheśa</s> (the Great Lord) — || SivSV 1.12:8 ||

body.text: * ārādhanaparā tadvad icchā śaktis tu yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.12:9 ||
body.translated_text: Likewise, <s>icchā śakti</s> (will-power) of the <s>yogī</s>. || SivSV 1.12:9 ||

body.text: * ayam eva sphuṭaḥ pāṭho dṛṣṭo 'nuttaradaiśikaiḥ || SivSV_1.12:10 ||
body.translated_text: This is the clear reading seen by the teachers of the <s>Anuttara</s> (Supreme) [tradition]. || SivSV 1.12:10 ||

body.text: * vyākhyātaś ca paraiḥ śaktitametipaṭhanāt punaḥ || SivSV_1.12:11 ||
body.translated_text: And it has been explained by others; moreover, from the reading '<s>śaktitama</s>' (most powerful), (SivSV 1.12:11)
the excellence of that <s>śakti</s> (power) has been expounded in terms of knowledge and action. (SivSV 1.12:12)
Thus, for the <s>yogī</s> endowed with the power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>) of such potency, (SivSV 1.12:13)
The visible [universe] is the body. (SivS 1.13)

children.text: * yad yad dṛśyam aśeṣaṃ tac charīraṃ tasya yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.13:1 ||
children.translated_text: Whatever is visible, all of that without exception is the body of that <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.13:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * aham ity apṛthaktvena pativat pratibhāsanāt || SivSV_1.13:2 ||
body.translated_text: because it shines as 'I' in non-difference, just as [the body shines] for the Lord. (SivSV 1.13:2)
The body — [encompassing] the physical body, intellect, vital breath, and the void — like a pot and so forth, (SivSV 1.13:3)

body.text: * dṛśyam evāsya paśuvat draṣṭṛtvena na bhāsate || SivSV_1.13:4 ||
body.translated_text: is merely visible for him; like a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>), it does not shine as the seer. (SivSV 1.13:4)

body.text: * evaṃ dehe ca bāhye ca sarvatraivāsya yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.13:5 ||
body.translated_text: Thus, in the body and in the external [world], everywhere for this <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.13:5)
by the analogy of the pigment within a peacock's egg, there arises non-dual cognition. (SivSV 1.13:6)

body.text: * dṛśyaṃ śarīratām eti śarīraṃ cāpi dṛśyatām || SivSV_1.13:7 ||
body.translated_text: The visible becomes the body, and the body also becomes the visible, (SivSV 1.13:7)

body.text: * ity uktaṃ yogino yat tan na durghaṭam itīryate || SivSV_1.13:8 ||
body.translated_text: this is what has been stated regarding the <s>yogī</s>; it is said that this is not difficult to accomplish. (SivSV 1.13:8)
In the heart, through the contact of consciousness (<s>citta</s>), there is the perception of the sleep-nature of the visible, (SivSV 1.13:9)

body.text: * hṛdayaṃ tad vijānīyād viśvasyāyatanaṃ mahat || SivSV_1.13:10 ||
body.translated_text: one should know that heart as the great abode of the universe. (SivSV 1.13:10)
By the stated principle, the heart is the ground and foundation of the repose of the universe, (SivSV 1.13:11)

body.text: * svasaṃvit tatra saṃghaṭṭaś cittasya calataḥ sataḥ || SivSV_1.13:12 ||
body.translated_text: self-awareness (<s>svasaṃvit</s>) is there; the contact is of the mind which exists in motion, (SivSV 1.13:12)
the nature of being alert through the apprehension of identity with that. (SivSV 1.13:13)
Therefore, of the visible universe, which takes the form of blue, body, and so forth, (SivSV 1.13:14)
there is also the perception of its sleep-nature, its absence, and even of the void. (SivSV 1.13:15)

body.text: * svāṅgarūpeṣu bhāveṣu pramātā kathyate patiḥ || SivSV_1.13:16 ||
body.translated_text: The cognizer (<s>pramātā</s>) is called the Lord in respect to entities that are of the nature of his own limbs, (SivSV 1.13:16)

body.text: * iti śrīpratyabhijñoktanītyā patyur iva prabhoḥ || SivSV_1.13:17 ||
body.translated_text: thus, by the principle stated in the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, just as for the Lord, the master, (SivSV 1.13:17)
there is the manifestation of that as his own limbs, as it truly is. (SivSV 1.13:18)

body.text: * ukte 'py evaṃ prameye 'sminn upāyāntaram ucyate || SivSV_1.13:19 ||]
body.translated_text: Even though this object of knowledge has been thus stated, another means is now described. (SivSV 1.13:19)
Or, from contemplation of the pure principle, the power of the unbound. (SivS 1.14)

children.text: * śuddhaṃ tattvaṃ paraṃ vastu yat tat paraśivātmakam || SivSV_1.14:1 ||
children.translated_text: The pure principle (<s>śuddha tattva</s>) is the supreme reality, which is of the nature of <s>Paraśiva</s>, (SivSV 1.14:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
its contemplation (<s>saṃdhāna</s>) is the meditation on the manifold world as being of that nature, (SivSV 1.14:2)

body.text: * tenaiva yasya paśvākhyā bandhaśaktir na vidyate || SivSV_1.14:3 ||
body.translated_text: by that very [contemplation], for whom the binding power called '<s>paśu</s>' (bound soul) does not exist, (SivSV 1.14:3)

body.text: * tat sadāśivavatso 'pi viśvasya jagataḥ patiḥ || SivSV_1.14:4 ||
body.translated_text: he, like <s>Sadāśiva</s>, though [still embodied], is the lord of the entire universe, (SivSV 1.14:4)
for this <s>yogī</s> who possesses the contemplation of the pure principle. (SivSV 1.14:5)
Deliberation (<s>vitarka</s>) is self-knowledge. (SivS 1.15)

children.translated_text: For the <s>yogī</s> whose bondage has been destroyed by the previously stated contemplation, <s>vitarka</s> (deliberation) is (SivSV 1.15:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * viśvātmā śiva evāham asmīty arthavicintanam || SivSV_1.15:2 ||
body.translated_text: the reflection on the meaning 'I am indeed <s>Śiva</s>, the Self of the universe,' (SivSV 1.15:2)

body.text: * etad eva sphuradrūpam ātmano jñānam ucyate || SivSV_1.15:3 ||
body.translated_text: this very [reflection], whose nature is radiant, is called knowledge of the Self. (SivSV 1.15:3)
Moreover, for this one who possesses the stated self-knowledge born of deliberation, (SivSV 1.15:4)
The bliss of the world is the joy of <s>samādhi</s> (meditative absorption). (SivS 1.16)

children.text: * lokyaṃ lokayitā ceti lokaś cetyacidātmani || SivSV_1.16:1 ||
children.translated_text: The perceivable, the perceiver, and consciousness — this is '<s>loka</s>' (world) in the non-conscious [realm], (SivSV 1.16:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * tattadrūpatayā tasmiṃ loke sphurati yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.16:2 ||
body.translated_text: in that world, in the form of each respective [entity], there shines forth for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.16:2)
the consciousness of object and subject is common to all embodied beings, (SivSV 1.16:3)

body.text: * yogināṃ tu viśeṣo 'yaṃ sambandhe sāvadhānatā || SivSV_1.16:4 ||
body.translated_text: but the distinction for <s>yogīs</s> is this: attentiveness in the relation [between subject and object], (SivSV 1.16:4)

body.text: * ity uktanītyā tat sarvam aham ity anusaṃhiteḥ || SivSV_1.16:5 ||
body.translated_text: by the stated principle, from the synthesis of all that as 'I,' (SivSV 1.16:5)

body.text: * ānando yo bhavaty antas tat samādhisukhaṃ smṛtam || SivSV_1.16:6 ||
body.translated_text: the bliss (<s>ānanda</s>) that arises within is known as the joy of <s>samādhi</s>. (SivSV 1.16:6)

body.text: * yat samādhisukhaṃ tasya svātmārāmasya yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.16:7 ||
body.translated_text: That which is the joy of <s>samādhi</s> of that <s>yogī</s> who delights in the Self, (SivSV 1.16:7)

body.text: * tad eva loke lokānām ānando 'ntarvicinvatām || SivSV_1.16:8 ||
body.translated_text: that itself is the bliss of the world for worldly beings who reflect within. (SivSV 1.16:8)

body.text: * vibhūtiyogam etasya darśayaty atha yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.16:9 ||]
body.translated_text: Now it is shown the practice of supernatural powers (<s>vibhūti</s>) of this <s>yogī</s>. (SivSV 1.16:9)
By contemplation of <s>Śakti</s> (power), the creation of bodies [at will]. (SivS 1.17)

children.text: * icchā śaktir umety ādisūtroktā śaktir asya yā || SivSV_1.17:1 ||
children.translated_text: The power of will (<s>icchā śakti</s>), which is <s>Umā</s>, as stated in the earlier sūtra — that <s>śakti</s> which belongs to him, (SivSV 1.17:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * saṃdhāne yoginas tasyās tanmayībhāvane sati || SivSV_1.17:2 ||
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogī</s> contemplates it, when he becomes one with it, (SivSV 1.17:2)
by its power, the creation of bodies fit for the respective desires is established, (SivSV 1.17:3)

body.text: * anyāś ca siddhayas tasya sambhavantīty udīryate || SivSV_1.17:4 ||]
body.translated_text: and other supernatural accomplishments (<s>siddhis</s>) also arise for him — thus it is declared. (SivSV 1.17:4)
Union with elements, separation of elements, and uniting of the entire universe. (SivS 1.18)

children.translated_text: Of the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) — body, intellect, vital breath, and void — which are of the nature of the cognizer, (SivSV 1.18:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * grāhyāṇāṃ sthāvarāṇāṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ paripoṣaṇam || SivSV_1.18:2 ||
body.translated_text: and of the cognizable, such as immovable [entities], <s>saṃdhāna</s> (union) means nourishment and integration, (SivSV 1.18:2)
separation (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) means dissociation for the pacification of afflictions such as disease, (SivSV 1.18:3)
and of the universe, which is distant in space, time, and so forth, (SivSV 1.18:4)
<s>saṃghaṭṭa</s> (uniting) means making directly perceptible through the eye and other senses, and so forth, (SivSV 1.18:5)

body.text: * etat sarvaṃ bhavec chaktisaṃdhāne sati yoginaḥ || SivSV_1.18:6 ||
body.translated_text: all of this occurs for the <s>yogī</s> when contemplation of <s>Śakti</s> takes place, (SivSV 1.18:6)

body.text: * yadā parimitāḥ siddhīr anicchan punar icchati || SivSV_1.18:7 ||
body.translated_text: when, not desiring limited accomplishments, he again desires (SivSV 1.18:7)

body.text: * viśvātmatāprathārūpāṃ parāṃ siddhiṃ tadāsya tu || SivSV_1.18:8 ||]
body.translated_text: the supreme accomplishment, which is of the nature of the manifestation of universal selfhood — then for him, (SivSV 1.18:8)
From the rise of pure knowledge (<s>śuddhavidyā</s>), the attainment of lordship over the collective [of powers]. (SivS 1.19)

children.translated_text: When the <s>yogī</s>, desiring the manifestation of universal selfhood, contemplates his own <s>śakti</s>, (SivSV 1.19:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yadā yogī tadā tasya sadāśivapadaspṛśaḥ || SivSV_1.19:2 ||
body.translated_text: then, for him who has touched the state of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, (SivSV 1.19:2)

body.text: * īśvaro bahir unmeṣo nimeṣo 'ntaḥ sadāśivaḥ || SivSV_1.19:3 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Īśvara</s> is the outward opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), and <s>Sadāśiva</s> is the inward closing (<s>nimeṣa</s>), (SivSV 1.19:3)
and there is co-referentiality of the 'I'-cognition and 'this'-cognition in <s>Sadvidyā</s> (pure knowledge), (SivSV 1.19:4)

body.text: * iti nītyā jagat sarvam aham eveti yā matiḥ || SivSV_1.19:5 ||
body.translated_text: by this principle, the cognition 'I alone am the entire universe' — (SivSV 1.19:5)

body.text: * sā śuddhā nirmalā vidyā tadīyād udayāt sphuṭam || SivSV_1.19:6 ||
body.translated_text: that is the pure, stainless <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge); from its arising, clearly, (SivSV 1.19:6)

body.text: * unmajjanāt sa cicchaktim ātmano nityam āmṛśet || SivSV_1.19:7 ||
body.translated_text: from its emergence, he would constantly apprehend the <s>cit-śakti</s> (power of consciousness) of the Self, (SivSV 1.19:7)

body.text: * yadā yogī tadā tasya cakreśatvam anuttaram || SivSV_1.19:8 ||
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogī</s> [does so], then his lordship over the collective (<s>cakreśatva</s>) is unsurpassed, (SivSV 1.19:8)
the sovereignty of <s>Maheśvara</s> is accomplished through the excellence of <s>samāveśa</s> (absorption) for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 1.19:9)
he who is both of the nature of the universal Self and transcendent, delighting in the Self, (SivSV 1.19:10)

body.text: * icchati svacchacidrūpo yadā yogī tadāsya tu || SivSV_1.19:11 ||]
body.translated_text: when the <s>yogī</s>, whose consciousness is transparent, wills it — then for him, (SivSV 1.19:11)
From contemplation of the great lake (<s>mahāhrada</s>), the experience of the power of <s>mantras</s>. (SivS 1.20)

children.translated_text: The supreme goddess (<s>parā bhaṭṭārikā</s>), consciousness (<s>saṃvit</s>), preceded by the power of will (<s>icchāśakti</s>), (SivSV 1.20:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
emitting the entire inner universe up to gross knowable objects, (SivSV 1.20:2)
of the cognizer — the inner and outer forms, the senses, and objects, (SivSV 1.20:3)
of the streams of <s>Khecarī</s> and other [energies], which have both external and internal forms, (SivSV 1.20:4)
being the impeller [of all these], due to the qualities of transparency, depth, and so forth, (SivSV 1.20:5)
[she is] the great lake (<s>mahāhrada</s>), pervading the universe, beyond space, time, and so forth, (SivSV 1.20:6)
from the inner contemplation of that, from the apprehension of identity [with it], (SivSV 1.20:7)
of the mass of sounds (<s>śabdarāśi</s>) whose nature is the manifestation from the letter 'a' to the letter 'kṣa,' (SivSV 1.20:8)
which causes agitation within the principles (<s>tattvas</s>) from earth to <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 1.20:9)
of <s>mantravīrya</s> (the power of mantra) which is the life-force of all <s>mantras</s>, (SivSV 1.20:10)
which consists in the apprehension of the supreme I-consciousness — there is clear experience. (SivSV 1.20:11)

body.text: * akhilaṃ vācakaṃ vācyam aham ity avamarśanam || SivSV_1.20:12 ||
body.translated_text: The apprehension of the entire signifier and signified as 'I' — (SivSV 1.20:12)

body.text: * yoginaḥ sāvadhānasya bhavatīty eva śiṣyate || SivSV_1.20:13 ||
body.translated_text: this arises for the <s>yogī</s> who is attentive — thus it is taught. (SivSV 1.20:13)

body.text: * sphuṭīkaromi saṃkṣepāt tat prameyaṃ puroditam || SivSV_1.20:14 ||
body.translated_text: I shall briefly clarify that object of knowledge stated above. (SivSV 1.20:14)

body.text: * mahāhrada iti proktā śaktir bhagavatī parā || SivSV_1.20:15 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>mahāhrada</s> (great lake) refers to the supreme divine <s>Śakti</s>, (SivSV 1.20:15)
'contemplation' (<s>anusaṃdhāna</s>) refers to the reflective awareness of identity with that, (SivSV 1.20:16)
'<s>mantravīrya</s>' (power of mantra) refers to the reflective awareness of the full I-consciousness, (SivSV 1.20:17)

body.text: * tadīyo 'nubhavas tasya sphuraṇaṃ svātmanaḥ sphuṭam || SivSV_1.20:18 ||
body.translated_text: its 'experience' (<s>anubhava</s>) is the clear radiance of one's own Self. (SivSV 1.20:18)
Thus, devoted to illuminating the <s>Śāmbhavopāya</s> (the means of <s>Śiva</s>), (SivSV 1.20:19)
the first awakening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), properly characterized by the unfolding of one's own nature, [is complete]. (SivSV 1.20:20)

children.translated_text: The mind (<s>citta</s>) is <s>mantra</s>. (SivS 2.1)

body.translated_text: <s>Śivasūtra</s>, Second Awakening (<s>Dvitīya Unmeṣa</s>)

children.translated_text: By which the supreme Self-principle is known and reflected upon — (SivSV 2.1:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
this is <s>citta</s> (mind): the reflective awareness of the radiant Self's grace and so forth, (SivSV 2.1:2)

body.text: * tad eva mantryate guptam abhedena vimṛśyate || SivSV_2.1:3 ||
body.translated_text: that very [mind] is 'mantried' — the hidden [reality] is reflected upon in non-duality, (SivSV 2.1:3)

body.text: * svasvarūpam aneneti mantras tenāsya daiśikaiḥ || SivSV_2.1:4 ||
body.translated_text: one's own true nature [is reflected upon] by this — therefore it is <s>mantra</s>, as explained by the teachers, (SivSV 2.1:4)
the quality of spontaneous resonance and pulsation through contemplation of the full I-consciousness, (SivSV 2.1:5)
and the quality of protection (<s>trāṇa</s>) through the destruction of <s>saṃsāra</s> — this is declared. (SivSV 2.1:6)
Through the apprehension of the <s>mantra</s>'s deity, having attained equality with that, (SivSV 2.1:7)

body.text: * ārādhakasya cittaṃ ca mantras taddharmayogataḥ || SivSV_2.1:8 ||
body.translated_text: the mind of the worshiper also becomes <s>mantra</s> through union with its qualities. (SivSV 2.1:8)
And of this stated <s>mantra</s>, whose nature is contemplation (<s>manana</s>) and protection (<s>trāṇa</s>), (SivSV 2.1:9)
Effort (<s>prayatna</s>) is the accomplisher. (SivS 2.2)

children.translated_text: Having the nature of the agent that arises from the steadfast contemplation of the stated <s>mantra</s>, (SivSV 2.2:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * prayatno 'ntaḥsvasaṃrambhaḥ sa eva khalu sādhakaḥ || SivSV_2.2:2 ||
body.translated_text: effort is the inner self-exertion; that indeed is the accomplisher (<s>sādhaka</s>), (SivSV 2.2:2)
because it is said to bestow unity between the <s>mantra</s>-reciter and the <s>mantra</s>-deity. (SivSV 2.2:3)
Of the <s>mantra</s>, which has such an accomplisher and such a goal, the previously stated (SivSV 2.2:4)

body.text: * vīryaṃ vistarataḥ samyag varṇyate 'tha salakṣaṇam || SivSV_2.2:5 ||]
body.translated_text: power (<s>vīrya</s>) is now properly described in detail, along with its characteristics. (SivSV 2.2:5)
The being of the body of knowledge is the secret of <s>mantra</s>. (SivS 2.3)

children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) is that whose nature is the realization of the supreme non-duality, (SivSV 2.3:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * śarīraṃ yasya bhagavān śabdarāśiḥ sa ucyate || SivSV_2.3:2 ||
body.translated_text: he whose body is the blessed aggregate of words (<s>śabdarāśi</s>) — he is spoken of, (SivSV 2.3:2)
his being (<s>sattā</s>) is of the nature of the full I-consciousness pervading all pathways (<s>adhvans</s>), (SivSV 2.3:3)
that very radiance is [the essence] of <s>mantras</s> whose nature is contemplation and protection, (SivSV 2.3:4)

body.text: * guptārthatāyā jananaṃ rahasyam iti kathyate || SivSV_2.3:5 ||
body.translated_text: the generation of hidden meaning is called the secret (<s>rahasya</s>). (SivSV 2.3:5)
This has been extracted from the <s>Tantrasāra</s> by the revered <s>Kṣemarāja</s>, (SivSV 2.3:6)
and properly described through concordant, authoritative [passages] proceeding in their own commentarial manner. (SivSV 2.3:7)

body.text: * samyag evaṃvidhaṃ mantravīryaṃ yeṣāṃ yathātatham || SivSV_2.3:8 ||
body.translated_text: For those for whom such <s>mantravīrya</s> (power of mantra), properly and as it truly is, (SivSV 2.3:8)
has been conveyed through the method of contemplation of the <s>mahāhrada</s> (great lake), and yet (SivSV 2.3:9)
by the will of the great Lord (<s>Maheśa</s>) alone, does not firmly enter the heart, (SivSV 2.3:10)

body.text: * na gacchaty atha tucchāyāṃ cittaṃ siddhau prarohati || SivSV_2.3:11 ||
body.translated_text: their mind then sprouts into a trifling accomplishment (<s>siddhi</s>), (SivSV 2.3:11)
arising from <s>bindu</s>, <s>nāda</s>, and so forth — for those <s>yogīs</s> of limited [attainment]. (SivSV 2.3:12)
In the womb [of ignorance], the expansion of mind is the dream of undifferentiated knowledge. (SivS 2.4)

children.translated_text: The womb (<s>garbha</s>) is ignorance (<s>akhyāti</s>), the great illusion (<s>Mahāmāyā</s>); in the accumulation of accomplishments of that nature, (SivSV 2.4:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * vikāso nāma cittasya tāvanmātre kṛtārthatā || SivSV_2.4:2 ||
body.translated_text: the expansion of mind means being satisfied with just that much, (SivSV 2.4:2)
that itself is undifferentiated knowledge (<s>aviśiṣṭā vidyā</s>), whose nature is partial knowing, (SivSV 2.4:3)
impure knowledge — that is the dream, filled with <s>vikalpa</s> (conceptual constructions), (SivSV 2.4:4)

body.text: * āgatā api tāḥ siddhīḥ khalīkṛtya yadā punaḥ || SivSV_2.4:5 ||
body.translated_text: but when, having set aside even those accomplishments that have come, (SivSV 2.4:5)

body.text: * avaṣṭabhnāty asau yogī parāṃ siddhiṃ tadāśnute || SivSV_2.4:6 ||]
body.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> firmly persists, then he attains the supreme accomplishment. (SivSV 2.4:6)
Upon the natural arising of [pure] knowledge, the state of <s>Śiva</s> is <s>Khecarī</s> (the one who moves in the space of consciousness). (SivS 2.5)

children.translated_text: Of <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), whose form was previously described, by the will of <s>Śaṃkara</s>, (SivSV 2.5:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
upon its natural arising — its spontaneous efflorescence, born of its own nature, (SivSV 2.5:2)
upon its emergence, [the yogī] being intent on immersion beyond trifling accomplishments, (SivSV 2.5:3)
the state which is non-different from the inner state of <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 2.5:4)
that very radiance, whose nature is the overflowing of perfect self-bliss, (SivSV 2.5:5)

body.text: * mudaṃ rātīty ato mudrā khecarī ca nabhaścarī || SivSV_2.5:6 ||
body.translated_text: gives (<s>rāti</s>) joy (<s>mud</s>) — therefore it is called <s>mudrā</s>; and <s>Khecarī</s> means 'moving in the sky [of consciousness],' (SivSV 2.5:6)
it is manifest everywhere for the <s>yogī</s> whose nature transcends the universe. (SivSV 2.5:7)
Thus, for the attainment of the power of <s>mantra</s> and <s>mudrā</s> of such potency, (SivSV 2.5:8)
The <s>guru</s> is the means. (SivS 2.6)

children.translated_text: The proper establishment of right knowledge, action, breath, <s>mantra</s>, and <s>mudrā</s> — (SivSV 2.6:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * gṛṇāty upadiśaty arthaṃ tadvīryaṃ cety ato guruḥ || SivSV_2.6:2 ||
body.translated_text: * He recites and teaches the meaning and its power — hence (he is called) <s>guru</s>.
* He himself, through revealing the pervasion of the power of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>,

body.text: * upāyaḥ kathyate sākṣād upeyaṃ paramaṃ prati || SivSV_2.6:4 ||
body.translated_text: * is stated to be the direct means (<s>upāya</s>) toward the supreme goal.

body.text: * yad vā guruḥ parā śaktir īśvarānugrahātmikā || SivSV_2.6:5 ||
body.translated_text: * Or, the <s>guru</s> is the supreme power (<s>parā śakti</s>), whose nature is the grace of the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>);
* by granting opportunity, that very (power) becomes the means.

body.text: * sa gurur matsamaḥ prokto mantravīryaprakāśakaḥ || SivSV_2.6:7 ||
body.translated_text: * 'That <s>guru</s> is declared equal to Me, the revealer of <s>mantra</s>-power' —

body.text: * ādimāntyavihīnās tu mantrāḥ syuḥ śaradabhravat || SivSV_2.6:8 ||
body.translated_text: * but <s>mantras</s> devoid of beginning and end would be like autumn clouds (empty of rain).

body.text: * guror lakṣaṇam etāvad ādimāntyaṃ ca vedayet || SivSV_2.6:9 ||
body.translated_text: * The characteristic of the <s>guru</s> is this: he should make known the beginning and end (of <s>mantras</s>).
* Thus, from the glory stated in the <s>Śrī Mālinīśāstra</s> and <s>Siddhatantra</s>,
* from the one who knows the beginning and end, whose nature is the spontaneous awareness of 'I' (<s>aham</s>),
* from that <s>guru</s> equal to the Supreme Lord (<s>Parameṣṭhin</s>), the highest means.]
Awakening to the circle of <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the alphabet-mother). // SivS 2.7 //

children.translated_text: * For one whose consciousness is continuously engaged in the contemplation of <s>mantras</s> and <s>mudrās</s>,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * bhavaty uktaguroḥ prītāt sādhakasyeti śiṣyate || SivSV_2.7:2 ||
body.translated_text: * from the pleased <s>guru</s> as described, the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) — thus it is taught.

body.text: * athādyās tithayaḥ sarve svarā bindvavasānagāḥ || SivSV_2.7:3 ||
body.translated_text: * Now the first vowels — all the <s>svaras</s> (vowels) ending in <s>bindu</s> (nasal point),
* within them, through conjunction with time (<s>kāla</s>), <s>Soma</s> (moon) and <s>Sūrya</s> (sun) are proclaimed.
* The <s>tattvas</s> (principles) from earth (<s>pṛthivī</s>) onwards up to <s>puruṣa</s> (soul), in the five

body.text: * kramāt kādiṣu vargeṣu makārānteṣu suvrate || SivSV_2.7:6 ||
body.translated_text: * groups (<s>vargas</s>) beginning with 'ka' and ending with 'ma,' O virtuous one,
* the four <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations) of wind, fire, water, and <s>Indra</s> (space),

body.text: * tadūrdhve śādi vikhyātaṃ purastād brahmapañcakam || SivSV_2.7:8 ||
body.translated_text: * above those, the well-known group beginning with 'śa,' the fivefold <s>Brahman</s> before it,

body.text: * amūlā tatkramāj jñeyā kṣāntā sṛṣṭir udāhṛtā || SivSV_2.7:9 ||
body.translated_text: * should be known from 'a' as the root, in that sequence; the creation ending in 'kṣa' is thus described.

body.text: * sarveṣāṃ caiva mantrāṇāṃ vidyānāṃ ca yaśasvini || SivSV_2.7:10 ||
body.translated_text: * Of all <s>mantras</s> and <s>vidyās</s> (sacred formulas), O illustrious one,

body.text: * iyaṃ yoniḥ samākhyātā sarvatantreṣu sarvadā || SivSV_2.7:11 ||
body.translated_text: * this is declared to be the womb (<s>yoni</s>, source) in all <s>tantras</s> at all times.
* Thus, by the principle stated in the <s>Śrī Triśikāśāstra</s>, the <s>Mātṛkā</s>
* is pregnant with sixteen vowels from 'a' to <s>visarga</s>.
* Hence, in the sequence of fifteen <s>tithis</s> (lunar days) beginning with the first <s>bindu</s> and ending with the last,
* adorned by the pair of <s>bindus</s> that are its essence and that which transcends it.

body.text: * ata eva jagat sarvaṃ sṛjaty antar anuttare || SivSV_2.7:16 ||
body.translated_text: * Hence it creates the entire universe internally in the <s>Anuttara</s> (the unsurpassed).
* Then, from the interior of the group of fifteen, with the five vowels extracted —

body.text: * a i u ṛ ḷ vinyāsaiḥ kādimāntaṃ ca vācakam || SivSV_2.7:18 ||
body.translated_text: * 'a,' 'i,' 'u,' 'ṛ,' 'ḷ' — through their arrangement, the signifier (words) from 'ka' to 'ma' and ending,
* and the signified, the cluster of <s>tattvas</s> from earth to <s>puruṣa</s>,
* differentiated into five groups of five, expanded into five sets of five.

body.text: * bahiś cānuttarād eva sṛjatī viśvam īdṛśam || SivSV_2.7:21 ||
body.translated_text: * Externally also, from the <s>Anuttara</s> alone, it creates the universe in this manner.

body.text: * vāyvagnisalilendrāṇāṃ kramād ya ra la vātmanām || SivSV_2.7:22 ||
body.translated_text: * Of wind, fire, water, and <s>Indra</s> — in order, having the nature of 'ya,' 'ra,' 'la,' 'va' —
* through the mutual conjunction of the triad called <s>Anuttara</s>, <s>Icchā</s> (will), and <s>Unmeṣa</s> (awakening),
* and also through the conjunction of the pair known as <s>Anuttara</s> and <s>ṣaṇḍha</s> (the neuter),
* of those that have arisen, designating <s>kalā</s>, <s>vidyā</s>, <s>māyā</s>, and <s>rāga</s>,
* through concealment of one's true nature and removal of full agency etc.,
* for the bound soul (<s>paśu</s>) whose (powers) are fragmentary, bestowing limited agency etc.,
* through blocking the ascent to the pure <s>tattvas</s> such as <s>śuddhavidyā</s> above <s>māyā</s>,

body.text: * mūlād adho 'varohasya nirodhāc ca triśaṇkuvat || SivSV_2.7:29 ||
body.translated_text: * and through blocking the descent below the root — like <s>Triśaṅku</s> (suspended between heaven and earth),
* for this one established in the middle, through the sustaining nature of the <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations),
* the regulation that gives rise to the determination of the existence and non-existence of things —

body.text: * kālo 'pi tāṃ mahāmāyāṃ svatantrām anuvartate || SivSV_2.7:32 ||
body.translated_text: * even Time (<s>kāla</s>) follows that independent great <s>Māyā</s>.
* Thus, through the stated principle, being connected with the regulation of time, of the sixfold nature,

body.text: * sphārayantī vapuḥ paścāt tadūrdhvaṃ śādipañcakam || SivSV_2.7:34 ||
body.translated_text: * expanding the form, then above that, the fivefold group beginning with 'śa,'
* the body of <s>Brahman</s> from <s>Sadyojāta</s> to <s>Keśāna</s> (Īśāna),
* consisting of the subtle forms of earth, water, fire, wind, and space,
* in sequence, having the nature of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s>, <s>Īśa</s> (Īśvara), <s>Sadāśiva</s>, <s>Śakti</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>,
* expanding outward the internal (reality) through the creative impulse of <s>visarga</s>.
* Since the phoneme 'kṣa' is the last, standing within the letters from 'ka' to 'sa,'
* therefore by 'a' and 'ha,' as 'aham' ('I'), in non-separation,
* the manifold universe is embraced by <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> and shines forth.

body.text: * asyās tv evaṃprabhāvāyāś cakraṃ yat tad ihoditam || SivSV_2.7:42 ||
body.translated_text: * Of this (Mātṛkā) of such power, the circle (<s>cakra</s>) that is mentioned here
* is the cluster of vibrating powers (<s>spandaśakti</s>) of <s>Anuttara</s>, <s>Icchā</s> (will), <s>Unmeṣa</s> (awakening), etc.
* Awakening (<s>saṃbodha</s>) to that is the inner unification with one's own Self, which is a mass of consciousness-bliss (<s>cidānanda</s>).
* Now, for one whose Self has been awakened by such awakening to the circle of <s>Mātṛkā</s>,]
The body is the oblation (<s>havis</s>). // SivS 2.8 //

children.text: * śūnyaṃ dhīḥ prāṇa ity etat sṛjyate kṣīyate 'pi ca || SivSV_2.8:1 ||
children.translated_text: * The void, intellect (<s>dhī</s>), and vital breath (<s>prāṇa</s>) — these are created and also destroyed;

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * sthairyam asti paraṃ dehāpekṣayā na tu tattvataḥ || SivSV_2.8:2 ||
body.translated_text: * there is relative stability in comparison to the (physical) body, but not in ultimate reality.

body.text: * ity uktanītyā śūnyādeḥ pramātā tv asya bhittibhūḥ || SivSV_2.8:3 ||
body.translated_text: * By the stated principle, the subject (<s>pramātā</s>) of the void etc. is their substrate;
* the body — gross, subtle, etc. — of the supreme <s>yogin</s>, in the fire of consciousness (<s>cidagni</s>),
* being offered, is called the oblation (<s>havis</s>), because through the submersion of its subjectivity,
* it gives rise to the emergence of the subject as fully luminous pure awareness.
* Thus, with the body as the oblation, the fire of awakened consciousness blazes upward.]
Knowledge is the food (<s>anna</s>). // SivS 2.9 //

children.text: * jñānaṃ bandha iti proktaṃ yat prāk tat parayoginaḥ || SivSV_2.9:1 ||
children.translated_text: * That which was previously stated as 'knowledge is bondage,' for the supreme <s>yogin</s>,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * anātmany ātmatājñaptir annaṃ grasyata ity ataḥ || SivSV_2.9:2 ||
body.translated_text: * the false identification of the Self in the non-self — that is the food which is devoured. Hence,

body.text: * kiṃ ca yad yat prakāśātmasvarūpāmarśanātmakam || SivSV_2.9:3 ||
body.translated_text: * moreover, whatever knowledge has the nature of awareness of one's own form as luminous
* is called food (<s>anna</s>) because it produces supreme delight.

body.text: * yadā tv avahitaḥ śaśvad yogī naivaṃ bhavaty asau || SivSV_2.9:5 ||
body.translated_text: * But when the <s>yogin</s> is not constantly attentive in this way,
* then even for one possessing knowledge, through the pride of (false) composure,]
Upon the dissolution of <s>vidyā</s> (pure knowledge), the vision of the dream arising from it (occurs). // SivS 2.10 //

children.text: * vidyeti jñānavisphārarūpā yā tu puroditā || SivSV_2.10:1 ||
children.translated_text: * <s>Vidyā</s> is that which was described earlier as having the nature of the expansion of knowledge,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* namely <s>śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge); upon its dissolution, its non-arising, its submersion,
* of the dream arising from it, born gradually from the dissolution of <s>vidyā</s>,
* of the dream that is rooted in difference, of the flood of thought-constructs (<s>vikalpa</s>), the vision
* — the emergence — occurs for this practitioner of the previously described supreme nature,
* who is prideful about his attentiveness — thus it is taught.
* Thus ends the second <s>unmeṣa</s> (awakening), illuminating the <s>śāktopāya</s> (the means through power).]

children.translated_text: The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is the mind (<s>citta</s>). // SivS 3.1 //

body.translated_text: <s>Śivasūtra</s>, Third <s>Unmeṣa</s> (Awakening)

children.translated_text: * Shaped by the entry of impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of specific enjoyable objects such as sound,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* inclined toward operations such as determination (<s>adhyavasāya</s>) of various things,
* supported by the modes (<s>vṛttis</s>) of <s>sattva</s> etc., consisting of intellect (<s>buddhi</s>), ego (<s>ahaṃkāra</s>), and mind (<s>manas</s>),
* the mind (<s>citta</s>), due to non-recognition of one's true nature as the stated consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>),
* wandering through various wombs in accordance with respective <s>karmas</s>,

body.text: * atatīty ata evātmā tataḥ so 'ṇuḥ prakīrtitaḥ || SivSV_3.1:6 ||
body.translated_text: * moves about (<s>atatī</s>) — hence it is called <s>ātman</s>; therefore it is proclaimed as the limited individual (<s>aṇu</s>).
* But there is no 'moving about' for the <s>Ātman</s> whose nature is pure awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>) alone;

body.text: * ataś caitanyam ātmeti dhīkriyātmakam ātmanaḥ || SivSV_3.1:8 ||
body.translated_text: * therefore 'consciousness is the <s>Ātman</s>,' having the nature of the activity of awareness — that is the true nature of the Self.

body.text: * viśvasvabhāvabhūtaṃ tat tāttvikaṃ rūpam īritam || SivSV_3.1:9 ||
body.translated_text: * That which has become the nature of the universe — that is declared to be its ultimate form.
* Now, due to the manifestation by its own freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>),

body.text: * saṃkocād aṇutāyogāc cittam ātmeti lakṣitam || SivSV_3.1:11 ||
body.translated_text: * through contraction, by association with limited individuality (<s>aṇutā</s>), the mind (<s>citta</s>) is designated as the <s>ātman</s>.
* Thus there is no contradiction between the previous and the later teachings;

body.text: * asya cittasvarūpasya dehāder ātmanas tv aṇoḥ || SivSV_3.1:13 ||]
body.translated_text: * of this (being) whose nature is the mind (<s>citta</s>), the self (<s>ātman</s>) is the limited individual (<s>aṇu</s>), beginning with the body etc.]
Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) is bondage. // SivS 3.2 //

children.translated_text: * Internally, having the activity of cognition such as the determination of pleasure etc. as objects,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* externally, directed toward objects such as blue, body, etc. that correspond to those (internal cognitions),
* consisting of the appearance of difference — that is the knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) of this limited being (<s>aṇu</s>), which is his bondage.

body.text: * tatpāśitatvād evāsāv aṇuḥ saṃsarati dhruvam || SivSV_3.2:4 ||
body.translated_text: * Because of being bound by that, this limited being (<s>aṇu</s>) certainly transmigrates.

body.text: * jñānaṃ prakāśakaṃ loke ātmā caiva prakāśakaḥ || SivSV_3.2:5 ||
body.translated_text: * Knowledge is illuminating in the world, and the Self also is illuminating;

body.text: * anayor apṛthagbhāvāj jñānī jñāne prakāśate || SivSV_3.2:6 ||
body.translated_text: * due to the non-difference of these two, the knower shines in knowledge.

body.text: * ity uktanītyā jñānaṃ ca svasvarūpaprakāśakam || SivSV_3.2:7 ||
body.translated_text: * By the stated principle, knowledge also illuminates one's own true nature,

body.text: * ātmavat tat kathaṃ tasya bandhakatvaprasaṅgitā || SivSV_3.2:8 ||
body.translated_text: * like the Self — so how can it have the role of being a binder?

body.text: * ity āśaṅkyāha yady evaṃ prasannāt parameśvarāt || SivSV_3.2:9 ||
body.translated_text: * Anticipating this objection, He says: If the gracious Supreme Lord (<s>Parameśvara</s>)

body.text: * pratyabhijñā bhavaty eṣā tadā satyaṃ tvadīritam || SivSV_3.2:10 ||
body.translated_text: * bestows recognition (<s>pratyabhijñā</s>), then indeed what you say is true;

body.text: * tanmāyāśaktito naiṣa vimarśo 'sya yadā tadā || SivSV_3.2:11 ||]
body.translated_text: * but when this reflective awareness (<s>vimarśa</s>) does not arise due to His <s>māyāśakti</s>, then (knowledge is bondage).]
Non-discrimination of the <s>tattvas</s> (principles) beginning with <s>kalā</s> is <s>Māyā</s>. // SivS 3.3 //

children.translated_text: * Of the <s>tattvas</s> from <s>kalā</s> to earth, which flash forth subtly within,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* having the nature of coverings (<s>kañcukas</s>), bestowing limited agency etc.,
* existing in the form of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) and as the gross body etc.,
* non-discrimination is the identification of oneself with them;

body.text: * saiva sammohinī māyā tattvākhyātimayaṃ jagat || SivSV_3.3:5 ||
body.translated_text: * that very (non-discrimination) is the deluding <s>Māyā</s>; the world consists of non-recognition of the <s>tattvas</s>.
* Therefore, for the pacification of this <s>māyā</s> produced by it, for this <s>yogin</s>,]
Dissolution of the <s>kalās</s> (parts) in the body. // SivS 3.4 //

children.translated_text: * In the gross (body) consisting of the great elements (<s>mahābhūtas</s>), in the subtle (body) having the nature of the <s>puryaṣṭaka</s>,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]

body.text: * mūlādisamanānte ca śarīre yoginaḥ pare || SivSV_3.4:2 ||
body.translated_text: * and in the supreme body of the <s>yogin</s>, from the <s>mūla</s> (root) to the end of <s>samanā</s>,

body.text: * kalānāṃ tatra bhāgānāṃ kāryāṇāṃ kāraṇe nije || SivSV_3.4:3 ||
body.translated_text: * of the <s>kalās</s> (parts), of those portions, of the effects in their own cause,
* dissolution is the reality of the sole fire of awareness (<s>saṃvid</s>), through contemplation of absorption (<s>layacintā</s>),

body.text: * dāhādyāmarśayuktyā vā dhyātavya iti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.4:5 ||
body.translated_text: * or through the practice of contemplating burning etc. — thus it is taught.

body.text: * evaṃ dhyānābhidhāno yaḥ saṃhāropāya īritaḥ || SivSV_3.4:6 ||
body.translated_text: * Thus the means of dissolution called <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) is stated;

body.text: * evam etat pradhānāṃś ca prāṇāyāmapuraḥsarān || SivSV_3.4:7 ||
body.translated_text: * likewise the principal (means), preceded by <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control),

body.text: * anyān samādhiparyantān upāyān darśayaty asau || SivSV_3.4:8 ||]
body.translated_text: * and other means up to <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) — these He demonstrates.]
Dissolution of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels), conquest of the elements, isolation from the elements, and separation from the elements. // SivS 3.5 //

children.translated_text: * These are to be practiced by the diligent practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) — thus it is taught.

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
* Dissolution of the <s>nāḍīs</s> (channels) carrying <s>prāṇa</s> etc. is achieved through restraint of breath (<s>prāṇasaṃyama</s>),
* through the production of the sequence of exhalation (<s>recaka</s>) etc., in the fire of <s>udāna</s>,
* bringing about absorption in the central channel (<s>madhyanāḍī</s>), through becoming one with it.

body.text: * bhūtānāṃ bhūjalādīnāṃ jayo yaḥ sa udīryate || SivSV_3.5:5 ||
body.translated_text: * The conquest of the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) — earth, water, etc. — that is declared.
* The <s>vāyavī dhāraṇā</s> (wind concentration) is at the thumb, the <s>āgneyī</s> (fire concentration) at the navel center,

body.text: * māheyī kaṇṭhadeśe tu vāruṇī ghaṇṭikāśritā || SivSV_3.5:7 ||
body.translated_text: * the <s>māheyī</s> (earth concentration) at the throat region, the <s>vāruṇī</s> (water concentration) at the uvula,
* the <s>ākāśa dhāraṇā</s> (space concentration) at the crown of the head — it is said to grant all <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers).
* Thus through the <s>dhāraṇās</s> (concentrations) stated in the <s>Svacchandaśāstra</s>, mastery is achieved.

body.text: * bhūtebhyaḥ kila kaivalyaṃ cittapratyāhṛtis tataḥ || SivSV_3.5:10 ||
body.translated_text: * Isolation (<s>kaivalya</s>) from the elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) is the withdrawal (<s>pratyāhāra</s>) of the mind from them;
* separation (<s>pṛthaktva</s>) is the state of being one with one's own pure, untouched Self.

body.text: * bhūtasaṃdhāna ityādisūtroktaṃ yat phalaṃ purā || SivSV_3.5:12 ||
body.translated_text: * The fruit stated in the earlier <s>sūtras</s> beginning with 'union of the elements' (<s>bhūtasaṃdhāna</s>),
* is achievable effortlessly for one who possesses the <s>śāmbhavopāya</s> (the means of <s>Śiva</s>);
* but it is achievable through effort by the <s>āṇavopāya</s> (the individual means) — this is the distinction.

body.text: * ity evaṃ dehaśuddhyādyaiḥ samādhyantaiś ca yā bhavet || SivSV_3.5:15 ||
body.translated_text: * Thus, through purification of the body etc. and other means up to <s>samādhi</s>, whatever

body.text: * siddhiḥ sā mohavaraṇān nātmajñānād itīryate || SivSV_3.5:16 ||]
body.translated_text: * <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) arises, that is from the covering of delusion (<s>moha</s>), not from Self-knowledge — so it is stated.]
<s>Siddhi</s> (supernatural power) arises from the covering of delusion (<s>mohāvaraṇa</s>). // SivS 3.6 //

children.text: * moho vimohinī māyā tatkṛtāvaraṇāt kila || SivSV_3.6:1 ||
children.translated_text: * Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is the deluding <s>Māyā</s>; from the covering produced by it, indeed,

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārtika</s>:]
Through the previously stated means of <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) and others, the <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) would be limited, || SivSV 3.6:2 ||

body.text: * tattattattvopabhogātmā na tv asya paracitprathā || SivSV_3.6:3 ||
body.translated_text: Having the nature of enjoyment of this or that <s>tattva</s> — but not the manifestation of supreme consciousness. || SivSV 3.6:3 ||
For one whose delusion has been destroyed, again in <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) and in the waking state, || SivSV 3.6:4 ||
Resorting to the middle <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), between the paths of <s>prāṇa</s> (inhalation) and <s>apāna</s> (exhalation), || SivSV 3.6:5 ||

body.text: * ālambya jñānaśaktiṃ ca tatsthaṃ caivāsanaṃ labhet || SivSV_3.6:6 ||
body.translated_text: And taking support of the power of knowledge (<s>jñāna-śakti</s>), one attains the seat (<s>āsana</s>) established therein. || SivSV 3.6:6 ||

body.text: * prāṇādisthūlabhāvaṃ tu tyaktvā sūkṣmam athāntaram || SivSV_3.6:7 ||
body.translated_text: Abandoning the gross state of <s>prāṇa</s> and the rest, and then the subtle inner [state], || SivSV 3.6:7 ||

body.text: * sūkṣmātītaṃ tu paramaṃ spandanaṃ labhyate yataḥ || SivSV_3.6:8 ||
body.translated_text: One attains the supreme vibration (<s>spandana</s>) that transcends even the subtle; || SivSV 3.6:8 ||

body.text: * prāṇāyāmaḥ sa uddiṣṭo yasmān na cyavate punaḥ || SivSV_3.6:9 ||
body.translated_text: That is designated as <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control), from which one never falls again. || SivSV 3.6:9 ||

body.text: * śabdādiguṇavṛttir yā cetasā hy anubhūyate || SivSV_3.6:10 ||
body.translated_text: The activity of the qualities such as sound and other [sense objects] that is experienced by the mind — || SivSV 3.6:10 ||

body.text: * tyaktvā tāṃ paramaṃ dhāma praviśet tatsvacetasā || SivSV_3.6:11 ||
body.translated_text: Abandoning that, one should enter the supreme abode through one's own consciousness; || SivSV 3.6:11 ||
This is declared to be <s>pratyāhāra</s> (withdrawal of the senses), which cuts the bonds of existence. || SivSV 3.6:12 ||

body.text: * dhīguṇān samatikramya nirdhyeyaṃ cāvyayaṃ vibhum || SivSV_3.6:13 ||
body.translated_text: Having transcended the qualities of the intellect, [one should] meditate upon the imperishable, all-pervading, || SivSV 3.6:13 ||

body.text: * dhyātvā dhyeyaṃ svasaṃvedyaṃ dhyānaṃ tac ca vidur budhāḥ || SivSV_3.6:14 ||
body.translated_text: Object-free [reality]; having meditated on that which is to be meditated upon as self-experienced — the wise know that as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). || SivSV 3.6:14 ||

body.text: * dhāraṇā paramātmatvaṃ dhāryate yena sarvadā || SivSV_3.6:15 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is that by which the nature of the supreme self is always held — || SivSV 3.6:15 ||
That is designated as <s>dhāraṇā</s>, which destroys the bonds of worldly existence. || SivSV 3.6:16 ||

body.text: * svaparastheṣu bhūteṣu jagaty asmin samānadhīḥ || SivSV_3.6:17 ||
body.translated_text: Having equal understanding toward beings in oneself and in others in this world — || SivSV 3.6:17 ||

body.text: * śivo 'ham advitīyo 'haṃ samādhiḥ sa paraḥ smṛtaḥ || SivSV_3.6:18 ||
body.translated_text: 'I am <s>Śiva</s>, I am non-dual' — that is remembered as the supreme <s>samādhi</s> (absorption). || SivSV 3.6:18 ||
Thus, through the stages described by <s>Bhaṭṭāraka</s> in the <s>Mṛtyujit Tantra</s> (Tantra of Conquering Death), || SivSV 3.6:19 ||
Beginning with <s>prāṇa-saṃyama</s> (breath restraint) and culminating in <s>samādhi</s>, through progressive stages, || SivSV 3.6:20 ||
Absorption into the supreme principle indeed occurs — thus it is stated. || SivSV 3.6:21 ||
<s>Mohajayād anantābhogāt sahajavidyājayaḥ</s> (Through the conquest of delusion, from infinite expansion, there is the attainment of innate knowledge) // SivS 3.7 //

children.text: * moho māyā nijākhyātis tajjayāt tatparābhavāt || SivSV_3.7:1 ||
children.translated_text: Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is <s>Māyā</s>, the non-recognition of one's own [nature]; from its conquest, from its defeat, || SivSV 3.7:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The infinite [expansion] that arises from the sun of upsurge (<s>udyama</s>), extending to the cessation of impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>) — || SivSV 3.7:2 ||

body.text: * ābhogo yasya vistāra īdṛśād darśitātmanaḥ || SivSV_3.7:3 ||
body.translated_text: Whose expansion (<s>ābhoga</s>) is such a vastness, for one whose nature has been thus revealed, || SivSV 3.7:3 ||

body.text: * bhavet sahajavidyāyā jayo lābho yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.7:4 ||
body.translated_text: There occurs the conquest — the attainment — of <s>sahajavidyā</s> (innate knowledge) for the <s>yogī</s>. || SivSV 3.7:4 ||
Thus, for one in whom the great dawn of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge) has arisen through the conquest of delusion, || SivSV 3.7:5 ||
<s>Jāgrad dvitīyakaraḥ</s> (Waking is the second ray) // SivS 3.8 //

children.translated_text: Having enjoyed the innate knowledge (<s>sahajavidyā</s>), in the support of oneness with that, || SivSV 3.8:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * jāgarūkaḥ sadā yogī jāgrad ity ayam ucyate || SivSV_3.8:2 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s>, always awake, is called '<s>jāgrat</s>' (waking). || SivSV 3.8:2 ||
In relation to the complete I-consciousness whose nature is full self-awareness (<s>ahaṃ-vimarśa</s>), the world || SivSV 3.8:3 ||

body.text: * dvitīyam idam ākāraṃ karo yasya svadīdhitiḥ || SivSV_3.8:4 ||
body.translated_text: Is this second form; the 'ray' (<s>kara</s>) is its own radiance — || SivSV 3.8:4 ||
He becomes such — one for whom the universe has become his own ray. || SivSV 3.8:5 ||
Such is this [yogī], whose mind is always immersed in the awareness of his own self. || SivSV 3.8:6 ||
<s>Nartaka ātmā</s> (The self is the dancer) // SivS 3.9 //

children.translated_text: He dances — [the stages], supported by one's own true nature concealed within, || SivSV 3.9:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
By his own will, upon the wall of his own consciousness, through the play of his own vibration, || SivSV 3.9:2 ||
The various stages in the form of waking, dream, and deep sleep || SivSV 3.9:3 ||

body.text: * ābhāsayati yat tasmād ātmā nartaka ucyate || SivSV_3.9:4 ||
body.translated_text: He manifests; therefore the <s>Ātman</s> (self) is called the dancer. || SivSV 3.9:4 ||
For this <s>yogī</s> who is the dancer of the cosmic drama, || SivSV 3.9:5 ||
The world-teacher (<s>Jagadguru</s>) declares the stage where the stages [of the dance] are assumed: || SivSV 3.9:6 ||
<s>Raṅgo 'ntarātmā</s> (The stage is the inner self) // SivS 3.10 //

children.translated_text: That in which [the self] takes delight, with a nature eager for the play of the cosmic drama — || SivSV 3.10:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Thus the 'stage' (<s>raṅga</s>) is the inner self (<s>antarātmā</s>), the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) having the nature of <s>puryaṣṭaka</s> (subtle body). || SivSV 3.10:2 ||
The <s>yogī</s>, having established his footing there, through the play of his own senses' vibration, || SivSV 3.10:3 ||
Would illuminate the cosmic drama [extending] from <s>Sadāśiva</s> to earth. || SivSV 3.10:4 ||
On this stage which is the inner body, as he dances within his own inner self, || SivSV 3.10:5 ||
<s>Prekṣakāṇi indriyāṇi</s> (The senses are the spectators) // SivS 3.11 //

children.translated_text: The spectators — [the senses] whose body manifests the drama of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence), || SivSV 3.11:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The senses such as the eye, etc., inwardly experience wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) for the <s>yogī</s>. || SivSV 3.11:2 ||
Thus, for the <s>yogī</s> whose wheel of senses has become the spectators, || SivSV 3.11:3 ||
<s>Dhīvaśāt sattvasiddhiḥ</s> (Through the power of intellect, attainment of being) // SivS 3.12 //

children.translated_text: <s>Dhī</s> (intellect) is the understanding skilled in the reflective awareness of the true nature of one's own consciousness; || SivSV 3.12:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
By its power, the <s>sattva</s> (being/vibration) that revolves within, || SivSV 3.12:2 ||

body.text: * sphurattārūpiṇaḥ siddhir abhivyaktiḥ sphuṭaṃ bhavet || SivSV_3.12:3 ||
body.translated_text: Having the form of luminous manifestation — its <s>siddhi</s> (attainment) is the clear manifestation. || SivSV 3.12:3 ||
Thus, through the glory of attaining the <s>sattva</s> (being) whose nature is one's own luminous self, || SivSV 3.12:4 ||
<s>Siddhaḥ svatantrabhāvaḥ</s> (Accomplished is the state of freedom) // SivS 3.13 //

children.text: * siddhaḥ sampanna evāsya bhavet paramayoginaḥ || SivSV_3.13:1 ||
children.translated_text: 'Accomplished' (<s>siddha</s>) means fully attained — for this supreme <s>yogī</s>, || SivSV 3.13:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The state of freedom (<s>svatantra-bhāva</s>) is characterized by innate omniscience and omnipotence. || SivSV 3.13:2 ||
The freedom of the sovereign one, capable of bringing the entire universe under one's own control, || SivSV 3.13:3 ||
The state of freedom itself of this one whose self is filled with his own bliss. || SivSV 3.13:4 ||
<s>Yathā tatra tathānyatra</s> (As there, so elsewhere) // SivS 3.14 //

children.text: * yatra svābhāvike dehe sphuṭībhūtā svatantratā || SivSV_3.14:1 ||
children.translated_text: Where, in one's own natural body, freedom has become fully manifest, || SivSV 3.14:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yathā tatra tathānyatra dehe bhavati yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.14:2 ||
body.translated_text: As there, so elsewhere — in [other] bodies, it becomes so for the <s>yogī</s>. || SivSV 3.14:2 ||
For the one who is united [with consciousness], the full I-consciousness manifests. || SivSV 3.14:3 ||

body.text: * na caivam apy udāsīnena bhāvyaṃ yogināpi tu || SivSV_3.14:4 ||]
body.translated_text: Yet even so, the <s>yogī</s> should not remain indifferent; || SivSV 3.14:4 ||
<s>Bījāvadhānam</s> (Attention to the seed) // SivS 3.15 //

children.text: * sphurattātmā parā śaktir bījaṃ viśvasya kāraṇam || SivSV_3.15:1 ||
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>Śakti</s> (power) whose nature is luminous manifestation — the seed (<s>bīja</s>), the cause of the universe; || SivSV 3.15:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Attention (<s>avadhāna</s>) therein is the repeated immersion of the mind [in that]; || SivSV 3.15:2 ||

body.text: * yoginā sāvadhānena kartavyam iti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.15:3 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>yogī</s> should perform this with attention — thus it is taught. || SivSV 3.15:3 ||
Such a great <s>yogī</s>, attentive to the supreme <s>Śakti</s>, || SivSV 3.15:4 ||
<s>Āsanasthaḥ sukhaṃ hrade nimajjati</s> (Seated [in that posture], one plunges into the lake with ease) // SivS 3.16 //

children.text: * āsyate sthīyate yasminn aikātmyeneti cāsanam || SivSV_3.16:1 ||
children.translated_text: That in which one sits and abides in oneness — that is the seat (<s>āsana</s>); || SivSV 3.16:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * śāktaṃ balaṃ yat tatrasthas tadevāntaḥ parāmṛśan || SivSV_3.16:2 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>śākta bala</s> (power of Śakti) that is there — abiding there, reflecting upon that very [power] within, || SivSV 3.16:2 ||
The <s>yogī</s>, freed from the exertion of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration), and the like, || SivSV 3.16:3 ||
Which is the cause of the expansion of the great currents of <s>Khecarī</s> and other [mudrās], || SivSV 3.16:4 ||
In the lake endowed with qualities of clarity and others, filled with one's own bliss, || SivSV 3.16:5 ||
In the full ocean of consciousness, on the island of this-and-that, || SivSV 3.16:6 ||
Having abandoned all [other] means, one plunges in with ease. || SivSV 3.16:7 ||
Through the devouring of the body and the rest, one clearly becomes one with that [consciousness]. || SivSV 3.16:8 ||
Thus, having attained through <s>Āṇavopāya</s> (the individual means), through the conquest of delusion, || SivSV 3.16:9 ||
Through the excellence of the <s>Śākta</s> absorption arising from the emergence of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge), || SivSV 3.16:10 ||
Through deep immersion in the lake of supreme bliss made one's own, || SivSV 3.16:11 ||
The best of practitioners, possessing the glory of the state of <s>Śāmbhava</s> (pertaining to Śiva) that spontaneously shines forth. || SivSV 3.16:12 ||
<s>Svamātrā-nirmāṇam āpādayati</s> (He brings about the creation of his own measure) // SivS 3.17 //

children.translated_text: One's own '<s>mātrā</s>' (measure) — of consciousness of the previously described nature — || SivSV 3.17:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Is the contracted portion of limited selfhood, characterized as the knowable and the knower; || SivSV 3.17:2 ||
Bringing about its 'creation' (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) is perceiving it as having been created [by oneself]; || SivSV 3.17:3 ||

body.text: * sampādayati yogīndro yatheṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam icchayā || SivSV_3.17:4 ||
body.translated_text: The supreme <s>yogī</s> accomplishes this clearly, as desired, by will. || SivSV 3.17:4 ||
Thus, for the <s>yogī</s> who has the universal form arising from such power, || SivSV 3.17:5 ||

body.text: * punarjanmādisambandho na kaścid iti kathyate || SivSV_3.17:6 ||]
body.translated_text: There is no connection with rebirth and the like — thus it is stated. || SivSV 3.17:6 ||
<s>Vidyā-avināśe janma-vināśaḥ</s> (Through the non-destruction of <s>vidyā</s>, there is the destruction of [re]birth) // SivS 3.18 //

children.text: * vidyeti sahajā tasyā avināśaḥ sadodayaḥ || SivSV_3.18:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vidyā</s> means the innate [knowledge]; its non-destruction (<s>avināśa</s>) is its constant arising; || SivSV 3.18:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Through that alone, of the birth [i.e., the assemblage] accompanied by ignorance and associated with various <s>karmas</s>, || SivSV 3.18:2 ||
Of the collection consisting of body, <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath), mind, intellect, etc., of [that] birth — || SivSV 3.18:3 ||

body.text: * vināśo mūlavidhvaṃso bhavaty asyeti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.18:4 ||
body.translated_text: The destruction, the uprooting from the root, occurs — thus it is taught. || SivSV 3.18:4 ||

body.text: * yadā tu śuddhavidyāyāḥ svarūpaṃ tasya majjati || SivSV_3.18:5 ||
body.translated_text: But when the true nature of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge) sinks [i.e., is submerged], || SivSV 3.18:5 ||
Then the powers arise precisely for his delusion. || SivSV 3.18:6 ||
<s>Kavargādiṣu māheśvaryādyāḥ paśumātaraḥ</s> (In the consonant groups beginning with 'ka', <s>Māheśvarī</s> and others are the mothers of the bound) // SivS 3.19 //

children.translated_text: Abiding in the consonant groups beginning with 'ka', having assumed the role of presiding deities, || SivSV 3.19:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
<s>Māheśvarī</s> and the others, stated to be within the openings of consciousness, || SivSV 3.19:2 ||
Entering the bound souls (<s>paśus</s>), the knowing subjects, || SivSV 3.19:3 ||
In the various domains of cognition, || SivSV 3.19:3 ||
Through the pervasion of the respective words, through delusion, they are the mothers of the bound (<s>paśu-mātaraḥ</s>); || SivSV 3.19:4 ||
Concealing one's own true nature, which is a mass of consciousness and bliss, || SivSV 3.19:5 ||

body.text: * atimānaṃ vivṛṇvānāḥ śarīrādau jaḍe 'pi ca || SivSV_3.19:6 ||
body.translated_text: And revealing excessive pride in the body and other inert [things] — || SivSV 3.19:6 ||

body.text: * paśuvatsādhakam api pramattaṃ mohayanty amūḥ || SivSV_3.19:7 ||
body.translated_text: These [mothers] delude even the practitioner, like a bound soul, when he is inattentive. || SivSV 3.19:7 ||

body.text: * tasmād bhāvyaṃ sadānena sāvadhānena yoginā || SivSV_3.19:8 ||
