body.translated_text: Therefore, this <s>yogī</s> should always practice with attention. || SivSV 3.19:8 ||

body.text: * uktaṃ sāmānyato jñānādhiṣṭhānaṃ mātṛkety ataḥ || SivSV_3.19:9 ||
body.translated_text: It was stated generally that '<s>Mātṛkā</s> is the basis of knowledge'; therefore, || SivSV 3.19:9 ||

body.text: * idaṃ tu prāptatattvo 'pi pramādyan sādhakaḥ punaḥ || SivSV_3.19:10 ||
body.translated_text: This [teaching] is that even a practitioner who has attained the truth, when he becomes careless, again || SivSV 3.19:10 ||

body.text: * paśvadhiṣṭhānabhūtābhir mohyate mātṛbhis tv iti || SivSV_3.19:11 ||
body.translated_text: Is deluded by the <s>Mātṛs</s> (Mothers) who are the basis of the bound state. || SivSV 3.19:11 ||

body.text: * yata evam ataḥ śuddhavidyā prāptāpi yuktibhiḥ || SivSV_3.19:12 ||
body.translated_text: Since this is so, even though <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge) is attained through many methods, || SivSV 3.19:12 ||

body.text: * bahvībhiḥ sā punar mauḍhyādy athāsya na vinaśyati || SivSV_3.19:13 ||
body.translated_text: If through bewilderment and other [faults] it does not perish again for him, || SivSV 3.19:13 ||

body.text: * tathā sarvāsv avasthāsu yukto bhūyād itīryate || SivSV_3.19:14 ||]
body.translated_text: Then he should remain united [with consciousness] in all states — thus it is stated. || SivSV 3.19:14 ||
<s>Triṣu caturthaṃ tailavad āsecyam</s> (The Fourth should be poured like oil into the three) // SivS 3.20 //

children.text: * triṣv iti proktarūpeṣu jāgarādiṣu tailavat || SivSV_3.20:1 ||
children.translated_text: Into the three — the previously described waking and other [states] — like oil, || SivSV 3.20:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The Fourth (<s>turya</s>) — the previously described [state] whose nature is the manifestation of <s>Śuddhavidyā</s> (pure knowledge) — || SivSV 3.20:2 ||

body.text: * turyaṃ dhāma sadāsecyaṃ yathā syāt tanmayaṃ trayam || SivSV_3.20:3 ||
body.translated_text: The abode of <s>Turya</s> should always be poured in, so that the three become pervaded by it; || SivSV 3.20:3 ||

body.text: * yathā tailaṃ kramāt svīyam āśrayaṃ vyāpnuyāt tathā || SivSV_3.20:4 ||
body.translated_text: Just as oil gradually pervades its support, so too [should the Fourth pervade the three states]. || SivSV 3.20:4 ||
Through the flashing [of awareness] at the beginning and end points of waking, etc., clearly, || SivSV 3.20:5 ||
One should moisten the middle phase as well with the nectar of <s>Turya</s>-bliss. || SivSV 3.20:6 ||
By the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>jāgrat</s>' (waking), previously, through the quality of upsurge (<s>udyama</s>), || SivSV 3.20:7 ||
For the supreme <s>yogī</s> endowed with the union of the wheel of powers, || SivSV 3.20:8 ||
In the domains of waking, dream, and deep sleep, which flow spontaneously of their own accord, || SivSV 3.20:9 ||
The arising of the expansion of <s>Turya</s> flowing forth from within was described. || SivSV 3.20:10 ||
By the <s>sūtra</s> beginning with '<s>tritaya</s>' (triad), [the dissolution] accomplished through <s>Śāmbhavopāya</s> (the means of Śiva), || SivSV 3.20:11 ||
Through the process of forceful digestion (<s>haṭhapāka</s>), the absorption of waking, dream, and deep sleep [was shown]. || SivSV 3.20:12 ||
By this [present] <s>sūtra</s>, through the method of <s>Āṇavopāya</s> (the individual means), || SivSV 3.20:13 ||
The triad of waking and other states, remaining like petals, || SivSV 3.20:14 ||
Should be sprinkled with the nectar of <s>Turya</s> — this distinction is declared. || SivSV 3.20:15 ||
And here the means for the pouring of the <s>Turya</s>-nectar is again stated: || SivSV 3.20:16 ||
<s>Magnaḥ svacittena praviśet</s> (Immersed [in that], one should enter through one's own mind) // SivS 3.21 //

children.translated_text: Having abandoned <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) and other gross, conceptual means, || SivSV 3.21:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Through one's own mind, one's own consciousness, in the form of non-conceptual [awareness], || SivSV 3.21:2 ||
Having the nature of the nectar of wonder (<s>camatkāra</s>) of inward-turned reflective awareness, || SivSV 3.21:3 ||
Immersed in the nectar of <s>Turya</s>, the subjecthood of one's own body, etc. — || SivSV 3.21:4 ||

body.text: * majjanena praśamayan praviśet tat samāviśet || SivSV_3.21:5 ||
body.translated_text: By submerging [that limited subjecthood], pacifying it, one should enter — one should become absorbed. || SivSV 3.21:5 ||
Thus, for one whose intellect has entered the supreme state, by the very nature of reality, || SivSV 3.21:6 ||

body.text: * yadā bhūyaḥ prasaraṇaṃ yogino jāyate tadā || SivSV_3.21:7 ||]
body.translated_text: When the expansion again arises for the <s>yogī</s>, then: || SivSV 3.21:7 ||
<s>Prāṇa-samācāre samadarśanam</s> (In the movement of <s>prāṇa</s>, equal vision) // SivS 3.22 //

children.translated_text: Of <s>prāṇa</s>, purified by the entry of the fragrance of the radiant <s>Śakti</s>, || SivSV 3.22:1 ||

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Through the strength of the intellect that fully opens and supports the dissolution of all knots, || SivSV 3.22:2 ||

body.text: * īṣad bahir mandamandaṃ cāre prasaraṇe sati || SivSV_3.22:3 ||
body.translated_text: when there is slight outward movement, a gentle spreading forth, (SivSV 3.22:3)
equally, due to the nature being a dense mass of consciousness, there is always the perception of non-difference, (SivSV 3.22:4)

body.text: * saṃvedanaṃ bhavaty arthāt sarvāvasthāsu yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.22:5 ||
body.translated_text: awareness arises by implication in all states for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.22:5)
the state beyond <s>turya</s> (<s>turyātīta</s>), attainable through the firm support of <s>turya</s>, not being apprehended, (SivSV 3.22:6)
at the junctures of the beginning and end, when only the <s>turya</s> [state] is experienced, (SivSV 3.22:7)

body.text: * āste yogī tadāmuṣya tāvan mātreṇa tuṣyataḥ || SivSV_3.22:8 ||]
body.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> remains — then, for him who is satisfied with just that much, (SivSV 3.22:8)
In the middle, there is inferior creation. (SivS 3.23)

children.text: * pūrvasyām aparasyāṃ ca koṭau turyaniṣeviṇaḥ || SivSV_3.23:1 ||
children.translated_text: For the one who dwells in the <s>turya</s> state at the beginning and end junctures, (SivSV 3.23:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
for that <s>yogī</s> who is sometimes negligent in his attentiveness, (SivSV 3.23:2)

body.text: * madhyāyām avaro 'śreṣṭhaḥ kutsitaḥ sarga āpatet || SivSV_3.23:3 ||
body.translated_text: in the middle, an inferior, not excellent, degraded creation may arise, (SivSV 3.23:3)

body.text: * vyutthānātmā tato yogī sāvadhānaḥ sadā bhavet || SivSV_3.23:4 ||
body.translated_text: which is of the nature of emergence [from absorption] — therefore the <s>yogī</s> should always be attentive. (SivSV 3.23:4)

body.text: * avaraprasave vṛtte hy evaṃ madhyapade punaḥ || SivSV_3.23:5 ||
body.translated_text: When inferior creation has occurred in the middle stage, (SivSV 3.23:5)
through the relish of firm support in <s>turya</s>, one should apprehend the state beyond <s>turya</s> (<s>turyātīta</s>). (SivSV 3.23:6)

body.text: mātrāsv apratyayasaṃdhāne naṣṭasya punar utthānam // SivS_3.24 //
body.translated_text: When there is the joining of non-cognition in the sense-objects, there is the re-arising of what was lost. (SivS 3.24)

children.text: * mātrāḥ padārthāḥ rūpādyās tāsv ebhiś cakṣurādibhiḥ || SivSV_3.24:1 ||
children.translated_text: <s>Mātrās</s> (sense-objects) are objects such as form and so forth; in them, by these eyes and other (SivSV 3.24:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
sense organs, <s>svapratyaya</s> (self-cognition) is the awareness of one's own respective cognizables, (SivSV 3.24:2)

body.text: * saṃdhānaṃ tu samastaṃ tad aham ity anusaṃhitiḥ || SivSV_3.24:3 ||
body.translated_text: and <s>saṃdhāna</s> (joining) is the synthesis of all that as 'I,' (SivSV 3.24:3)
when this is present, for the <s>turya</s> that was lost, driven away from the stated class [of experience], (SivSV 3.24:4)

body.text: * turyasya punar utthānaṃ bhūya unmajjanaṃ bhavet || SivSV_3.24:5 ||
body.translated_text: there is re-arising, a fresh emergence once again, (SivSV 3.24:5)
the fullness through the attainment of unity with that — this is taught regarding the lord of <s>yogīs</s>. (SivSV 3.24:6)
Thus, the practitioner-bull, with excellence of the arising absorption, (SivSV 3.24:7)
becomes equal to <s>Śiva</s>. (SivS 3.25)

children.translated_text: Through the excellence of the practice of <s>turya</s>, the state which is of the nature of <s>turyātīta</s> (beyond the fourth), (SivSV 3.25:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
having attained it, the practitioner, directly, with the Self of all worlds within, (SivSV 3.25:2)
with <s>Śiva</s>, who is resplendent with transparent, free-flowing consciousness and bliss, (SivSV 3.25:3)
becomes equal — and upon the falling away of the bodily portion, he becomes <s>Śiva</s> [himself]. (SivSV 3.25:4)

body.text: * arjitaṃ dīkṣayā dagdhaṃ bhaviṣyanti yamādibhiḥ || SivSV_3.25:5 ||
body.translated_text: That [<s>karma</s>] which was acquired and burnt by initiation (<s>dīkṣā</s>) — future [<s>karmas</s>] through restraints (<s>yamas</s>) and so forth, (SivSV 3.25:5)

body.text: * yenedaṃ sādhitaṃ yatra tadbhuktyā vinivartate || SivSV_3.25:6 ||
body.translated_text: that by which this [state] was accomplished, and where it ceases through its enjoyment, (SivSV 3.25:6)

body.text: * anekabhāvikaṃ karma dagdhaṃ bījam ivāgninā || SivSV_3.25:7 ||
body.translated_text: the manifold future <s>karma</s> is burnt like a seed [burnt] by fire, (SivSV 3.25:7)

body.text: * bhaviṣyad api saṃruddhaṃ yenedaṃ tad dhi bhogataḥ || SivSV_3.25:8 ||
body.translated_text: even the future [<s>karma</s>] is restrained — that by which this [liberation comes] is indeed through experience [of residual <s>karma</s>]. (SivSV 3.25:8)
By the stated principle, the ground for the experience of enjoyments already commenced (<s>prārabdha</s>), (SivSV 3.25:9)
the maintenance of the body is taught as his duty. (SivSV 3.25:10)
The activity of the body is [his] vow (<s>vrata</s>). (SivS 3.26)

children.text: * evaṃ pūrvoktayā nītyā śivatulyasya yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.26:1 ||
children.translated_text: Thus, by the previously stated principle, for the <s>yogī</s> who is equal to <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 3.26:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
whose nature is constantly devoted to the worship of his own Self which is ever <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 3.26:2)
nourished by the nectar of devotion, pure and transparent, shining within, (SivSV 3.26:3)

body.text: * bhavatpūjopayogāya śarīram idam astu me || SivSV_3.26:4 ||
body.translated_text: 'May this body of mine be for the purpose of worship of the Lord' — (SivSV 3.26:4)
by the direction stated by the glorious, transcendent <s>Utpala</s> (<s>Utpaladeva</s>), (SivSV 3.26:5)

body.text: * śivabhaktisudhāpūrṇe śarīre vṛttir asya yā || SivSV_3.26:6 ||
body.translated_text: his activity in this body, which is filled with the nectar of devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, (SivSV 3.26:6)

body.text: * vratam etad anuṣṭheyaṃ na tucchaṃ tasya dhāraṇam || SivSV_3.26:7 ||
body.translated_text: this is the vow (<s>vrata</s>) to be practiced — not a trivial observance for him. (SivSV 3.26:7)

body.text: * evaṃvidhasya tasyāsya yā yā svālāparūpiṇī || SivSV_3.26:8 ||]
body.translated_text: For this one of such nature, whatever speech is of the nature of [natural] conversation, (SivSV 3.26:8)
Ordinary conversation is <s>japa</s> (recitation). (SivS 3.27)

children.text: * mahāmantramayaṃ naumi rūpaṃ te svacchaśītalam || SivSV_3.27:1 ||
children.translated_text: 'I bow to Your form, which consists of the great <s>mantra</s>, transparent and cool, (SivSV 3.27:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
beautiful with unprecedented fragrance, overflowing with the essence of supreme nectar' — (SivSV 3.27:2)
by the direction stated by the teacher who composed the revered <s>Pratyabhijñā</s>, (SivSV 3.27:3)
for one who reflects upon his own Self as consisting of the natural, unartificial I-consciousness, (SivSV 3.27:4)

body.text: * yā yā svairābhilāpātmā kathā yāthārthyavādinaḥ || SivSV_3.27:5 ||
body.translated_text: whatever spontaneous conversation, the speech of the speaker of truth, (SivSV 3.27:5)

body.text: * bhūyobhūyaḥ pare bhāve bhāvanā bhāvyate hi yā || SivSV_3.27:6 ||
body.translated_text: the meditation that is meditated upon again and again in the supreme state, (SivSV 3.27:6)

body.text: * japaḥ so 'tra svayaṃ nādo mantrātmā japya īdṛśaḥ || SivSV_3.27:7 ||
body.translated_text: that is <s>japa</s> (recitation) here — the spontaneous resonance (<s>nāda</s>), of the nature of <s>mantra</s>, is what is to be recited thus. (SivSV 3.27:7)
Twenty-one thousand six hundred (SivSV 3.27:8)

body.text: * japo devyāḥ samuddiṣṭaḥ sulabho durlabho jaḍaiḥ || SivSV_3.27:9 ||
body.translated_text: [breaths] day and night is proclaimed as the <s>japa</s> of the Goddess — easy [for the awakened], difficult for the dull. (SivSV 3.27:9)
By the stated principle, that [recitation] which arises from the wealth of the reflective awareness of the universal Self-Lord, (SivSV 3.27:10)
because its nature is generation and protection, it is called <s>japa</s> (recitation). (SivSV 3.27:11)
And further, whatever conversation pertains to such a lord of <s>yogīs</s>, (SivSV 3.27:12)
that too is declared as <s>japa</s> for the people, by virtue of its connection with generation and protection. (SivSV 3.27:13)
And now his conduct (<s>caryā</s>) is stated, following proper boundaries. (SivSV 3.27:14)
The gift (<s>dāna</s>) is self-knowledge. (SivS 3.28)

children.translated_text: The direct realization of one's own Self, which is of the nature of the stated consciousness, (SivSV 3.28:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yat taj jñānaṃ tad evāsya dānaṃ yatnena dīyate || SivSV_3.28:2 ||
body.translated_text: that knowledge itself is his gift — it is given with effort, (SivSV 3.28:2)

body.text: * paripūrṇaṃ svarūpaṃ svaṃ dīyate khaṇḍyate bhidā || SivSV_3.28:3 ||
body.translated_text: one's own complete nature is given, difference is shattered, (SivSV 3.28:3)

body.text: * dāyate śodhyate rūpam ātmīyaṃ dīyate punaḥ || SivSV_3.28:4 ||
body.translated_text: the form is purified, one's own form is given [back], (SivSV 3.28:4)
the <s>Śiva</s>-Self, recognized through <s>pratyabhijñā</s> (recognition), is protected as one's own nature, (SivSV 3.28:5)

body.text: * dīyate ceti yatnena svātmajñānam anuttaram || SivSV_3.28:6 ||
body.translated_text: and the unsurpassed self-knowledge is given with effort, (SivSV 3.28:6)

body.text: * kṛpayā svātmaśiṣyebhyas tad anenaiva dīyate || SivSV_3.28:7 ||
body.translated_text: out of compassion, it is given to one's own disciples through this very [knowledge], (SivSV 3.28:7)

body.text: * evaṃ samyagvrataṃ proktaṃ japaṃ caryā ca pālayan || SivSV_3.28:8 ||
body.translated_text: thus, properly maintaining the stated vow (<s>vrata</s>), recitation (<s>japa</s>), and conduct (<s>caryā</s>), (SivSV 3.28:8)
equal to <s>Śiva</s>, always devoted to the worship of the <s>Śiva</s>-Self, (SivSV 3.28:9)
this very one is the great <s>yogī</s>, the foremost bearer of the great <s>mantra</s>, (SivSV 3.28:10)
the true teacher of principles to the inner circle of disciples, (SivSV 3.28:11)

body.text: * ity āha bhagavān īśo nityānugrahakārakaḥ || SivSV_3.28:12 ||]
body.translated_text: thus says the blessed Lord, the eternal bestower of grace. (SivSV 3.28:12)
He who is established in the circle of powers is the cause of knowledge. (SivS 3.29)

children.text: * avīn paśujanān pātīty avipaṃ śaktimaṇḍalam || SivSV_3.29:1 ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Avipa</s>' — that which protects (<s>pāti</s>) the flock (<s>avis</s>) of bound beings — is the circle of powers (<s>śaktimaṇḍala</s>), (SivSV 3.29:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
stated as <s>Māheśvarī</s> and others, the presiding deities of the letter-groups beginning with 'ka,' (SivSV 3.29:2)

body.text: * adhitiṣṭhati yaḥ svairam avipasthaḥ sa ucyate || SivSV_3.29:3 ||
body.translated_text: he who presides over them freely is called '<s>avipastha</s>' (established in the power-circle), (SivSV 3.29:3)

body.text: * jānātīty akhilaṃ tat jñā jñānaśaktir udīryate || SivSV_3.29:4 ||
body.translated_text: '<s>jña</s>' means he who knows everything — the power of knowledge is declared, (SivSV 3.29:4)

body.text: * tasyā hetus tayā śiṣyān pratibodhayituṃ kṣamaḥ || SivSV_3.29:5 ||
body.translated_text: he is the cause (<s>hetu</s>) of that [knowledge] — by that [power] he is capable of awakening disciples, (SivSV 3.29:5)
but another, being made dependent by the circle of powers, (SivSV 3.29:6)

body.text: * svātmany evāsamarthaḥ san katham anyān prabodhayet || SivSV_3.29:7 ||
body.translated_text: being incapable even regarding his own Self, how could he awaken others? (SivSV 3.29:7)

body.text: * yac chabdāpekṣayā sūtre tac chabdo 'dhyāhṛtaḥ svayam || SivSV_3.29:8 ||
body.translated_text: Whatever in the sūtra requires [additional] words, those words are self-supplied, (SivSV 3.29:8)

body.text: * caśabdo hy arthavācy atra yasmāj jñānaprabodhane || SivSV_3.29:9 ||
body.translated_text: the word 'ca' (and) here conveys the meaning — since [he is] the cause of the awakening of knowledge, (SivSV 3.29:9)

body.text: * yogī hetus tato dānam ātmajñānam itīritam || SivSV_3.29:10 ||
body.translated_text: the <s>yogī</s> is the cause; therefore 'the gift is self-knowledge' — thus it is stated. (SivSV 3.29:10)

body.text: * ity evam avipasthasya jñāhetor asya yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.29:11 ||]
body.translated_text: Thus, for this <s>yogī</s> who is established in the power-circle and is the cause of knowledge, (SivSV 3.29:11)
The universe is the aggregation of his own powers. (SivS 3.30)

children.text: * śaktayo 'sya jagat kṛtsnaṃ śaktimāṃs tu maheśvaraḥ || SivSV_3.30:1 ||
children.translated_text: 'His powers are the entire universe; the possessor of powers is <s>Maheśvara</s>' — (SivSV 3.30:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * ity āgamadiśā viśvaṃ svaśaktipracayo yathā || SivSV_3.30:2 ||
body.translated_text: by the direction of scripture (<s>āgama</s>), the universe is the aggregation of his own powers, just as (SivSV 3.30:2)
it is for <s>Śiva</s>, so also for this supreme <s>yogī</s> who is equal to Him, (SivSV 3.30:3)
of his own <s>śakti</s>, which is inseparable from his Self, which is of the nature of awareness, (SivSV 3.30:4)

body.text: * pracayaḥ sphuraṇārūpo vikāso viśvam iṣyate || SivSV_3.30:5 ||
body.translated_text: the aggregation (<s>pracaya</s>), the expansion in the form of radiance — that is considered the universe, (SivSV 3.30:5)

body.text: * na paraṃ sṛṣṭyavasthāyām amuṣya parayoginaḥ || SivSV_3.30:6 ||
body.translated_text: not only in the state of creation, for this supreme <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.30:6)
is the universe the aggregation of his own powers, but also following upon that, (SivSV 3.30:7)
maintenance and dissolution. (SivS 3.31)

children.text: * svaśaktipracayau proktau tāv apīty anuvartate || SivSV_3.31:1 ||
children.translated_text: they too are the aggregation of his own powers — thus it continues from the previous [sūtra], (SivSV 3.31:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
of the manifested universe, through one's own awareness consisting of action, (SivSV 3.31:2)
relative to each respective cognizer, for some time, in the form of 'this-ness,' (SivSV 3.31:3)

body.text: * yā sthitiś cinmayāhaṃtāviśrāntyātmā ca yo layaḥ || SivSV_3.31:4 ||
body.translated_text: that which is maintenance, and that which is dissolution — whose nature is repose in the consciousness-I, (SivSV 3.31:4)

body.text: * tāv ubhau yoginas tasya svaśaktipracayātmakau || SivSV_3.31:5 ||
body.translated_text: both of these, for that <s>yogī</s>, are of the nature of the aggregation of his own powers, (SivSV 3.31:5)

body.text: * vikasat saṃkucat sarvaṃ vedyaṃ yat saṃvidātmakam || SivSV_3.31:6 ||
body.translated_text: everything cognizable, expanding and contracting, is of the nature of consciousness, (SivSV 3.31:6)
otherwise, the cognition of that cognizable would be impossible. (SivSV 3.31:7)
Now, if in creation, maintenance, and dissolution, which are mutually different from each other, (SivSV 3.31:8)
the <s>yogī</s>'s own nature has become otherwise [i.e., subject to change], (SivSV 3.31:9)

body.text: * ity āśaṅkānivṛttyarthaṃ sūtram āha maheśvaraḥ || SivSV_3.31:10 ||]
body.translated_text: to dispel this doubt, the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>) states the [next] sūtra: (SivSV 3.31:10)
Even when those [creation, etc.] are occurring, there is no loss [of identity], due to the nature of being the knower. (SivS 3.32)

children.text: * teṣāṃ sṛṣṭyādibhāvānāṃ pravṛttāv apy anāratam || SivSV_3.32:1 ||
children.translated_text: Even when those states of creation and so forth are occurring unceasingly, (SivSV 3.32:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
even when they are emerging, for one who possesses the firmness of unwavering <s>yoga</s>-support, (SivSV 3.32:2)
and here there are two states, called 'being the effect' and 'being the agent,' (SivSV 3.32:3)

body.text: * kāryatā kṣayiṇī tatra kartṛtvaṃ punar akṣayam || SivSV_3.32:4 ||
body.translated_text: being the effect is perishable, but agency is imperishable, (SivSV 3.32:4)

body.text: * kāryonmukhaḥ prayatno yaḥ kevalaṃ so 'tra lupyate || SivSV_3.32:5 ||
body.translated_text: only the effort directed toward effects is lost here, (SivSV 3.32:5)

body.text: * tasmiṃl lupte vilupto 'smīty abudhaḥ pratipadyate || SivSV_3.32:6 ||
body.translated_text: when that is lost, the unwise thinks 'I am destroyed,' (SivSV 3.32:6)

body.text: * na tu yo 'ntarmukho bhāvaḥ sarvajñatvaguṇāspadam || SivSV_3.32:7 ||
body.translated_text: but the inward-facing state, which is the locus of the quality of omniscience — (SivSV 3.32:7)

body.text: * tasya lopaḥ kadācit syād anyasyānupalambhanāt || SivSV_3.32:8 ||
body.translated_text: its loss could never occur, due to the non-perception of anything else, (SivSV 3.32:8)
by the principle stated in the revered <s>Spandaśāstra</s>, for this <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.32:9)
there is no loss — due to the nature of being the self-knower, there is no falling away from one's own [nature], (SivSV 3.32:10)
due to the nature of the perceiver, arising from the wonder of the emergent <s>turya</s> state, (SivSV 3.32:11)

body.text: * nirāse tasya sṛṣṭyādeḥ sṛjyasyāpy aprakāśanāt || SivSV_3.32:12 ||
body.translated_text: if there were loss of that [identity], then creation and so forth, and even the created, would not be manifested, (SivSV 3.32:12)
for the <s>yogī</s> who is unshaken in the creation, maintenance, and dissolution of the universe. (SivSV 3.32:13)
The contemplation of pleasure and pain is external. (SivS 3.33)

children.translated_text: For the wise one who has transcended the subjectivity of body, vital breath, and so forth, (SivSV 3.33:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
his contemplation of pleasure and pain, born from contact with objects, (SivSV 3.33:2)
is external, in the form of 'this'-appearance, like blue, yellow, and so forth, (SivSV 3.33:3)

body.text: * ahaṃ sukhīti duḥkhīti lokavan na tv ahaṃtayā || SivSV_3.33:4 ||
body.translated_text: not as 'I am happy' or 'I am in pain' as for worldly beings, but not as I-consciousness, (SivSV 3.33:4)
by the principle of the sūtra 'the universe is the aggregation of his own powers,' (SivSV 3.33:5)
everything appears for him as veiled by I-consciousness, (SivSV 3.33:6)

body.text: * yogino laukikasyeva sukhādy eva na kevalam || SivSV_3.33:7 ||
body.translated_text: not only pleasure and so forth, as for an ordinary person, for the <s>yogī</s>, (SivSV 3.33:7)
having transcended the great delusion, having overcome the I-consciousness centered on body and so forth, (SivSV 3.33:8)
how could the king of <s>yogīs</s> be touched by pleasure and pain as worldly beings are? (SivSV 3.33:9)
Because the consciousness-subjectivity is ascending and the subtle-body position is receding, (SivSV 3.33:10)

body.text: * yato na tatsukhādyantas tata evaiṣa sādhakaḥ || SivSV_3.33:11 ||]
body.translated_text: since he is not internally [affected by] pleasure and so forth — for that reason this practitioner, (SivSV 3.33:11)
But one who is freed from those is the solitary one (<s>kevalī</s>). (SivS 3.34)

children.text: * tābhyāṃ mukto viśeṣeṇa yogīndro yat tayor yataḥ || SivSV_3.34:1 ||
children.translated_text: The lord of <s>yogīs</s>, freed especially from those two [pleasure and pain], because (SivSV 3.34:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * saṃskāreṇāpy asaṃspṛṣṭaḥ kevalī cinmayaḥ smṛtaḥ || SivSV_3.34:2 ||
body.translated_text: he is untouched even by their residual impressions (<s>saṃskāras</s>), is called <s>kevalī</s> (the solitary one), consisting of pure consciousness. (SivSV 3.34:2)
The word 'tu' (but) indicates a distinction, with reference to what is about to be stated, (SivSV 3.34:3)
thus also the one [mentioned] in the following sūtra, with reference to this sūtra, (SivSV 3.34:4)

body.text: * tad evāha tuśabdoktam antaraṃ candraśekharaḥ || SivSV_3.34:5 ||]
body.translated_text: that very distinction indicated by the word 'tu' is stated by <s>Candraśekhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>). (SivSV 3.34:5)
But one who is bound together by delusion is the <s>karmātmā</s> (soul bound by action). (SivS 3.35)

children.text: * mohaḥ svākhyātir ajñānaṃ tena yaḥ pratisaṃhataḥ || SivSV_3.35:1 ||
children.translated_text: Delusion (<s>moha</s>) is non-recognition (<s>akhyāti</s>), ignorance — one who is bound together by that, (SivSV 3.35:1)

body.translated_text: [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
having attained dense identification with it alone, he becomes the receptacle of suffering and so forth, (SivSV 3.35:2)

body.text: * tata eva sa karmātmā śubhāśubhakalaṅkitaḥ || SivSV_3.35:3 ||
body.translated_text: therefore he is the <s>karmātmā</s> (soul bound by action), stained by auspicious and inauspicious [deeds], (SivSV 3.35:3)
for even such a one as this, who is of the nature of respective <s>karmas</s>, when (SivSV 3.35:4)
through the unrestricted descent of grace (<s>śaktipāta</s>) from the great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>), there opens up (SivSV 3.35:5)

body.text: * svātantryayogaḥ sahajaḥ prādurasti tadāsya tu || SivSV_3.35:6 ||]
body.translated_text: a natural union with freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>), then for him — (SivSV 3.35:6)
Upon the concealment of difference, there is the capacity for another creation // SivS_3.36 //

children.translated_text: Of difference — born from the limited ego-sense concerning body, <s>prāṇa</s>, etc., || SivSV_3.36:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Having a nature suited to the <s>sakala</s> etc. state, deluded and enveloped by <s>kalā</s> etc., || SivSV_3.36:2 ||
Upon the concealment — even while remaining, through one's own opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), through the removal — || SivSV_3.36:3 ||
Through the manifestation of one's own greatness of identity with <s>mantra</s> and <s>mantreśvara</s>, || SivSV_3.36:4 ||
There would be the capacity for another creation for this supreme <s>yogin</s>, || SivSV_3.36:5 ||
So that creatorship of that which is to be created according to one's wish clearly manifests || SivSV_3.36:6 ||

body.text: * na caitad apy asaṃbhāvyaṃ sraṣṭṛtvaṃ yogino yataḥ || SivSV_3.36:7 ||]
body.translated_text: And this creatorship of the <s>yogin</s> is not impossible, since || SivSV_3.36:7 ||]
The power of doing (<s>karaṇaśakti</s>) [is established] from one's own experience // SivS_3.37 //

children.translated_text: From one's own self, from one's own experience, as in dream-imagination etc., || SivSV_3.37:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Doing (<s>karaṇa</s>) is the creation of one's own perceived objects, the known and the knower; || SivSV_3.37:2 ||
The power — the arising of that creatorship — is established through one's own awareness alone; || SivSV_3.37:3 ||

body.text: * sambhavantīṃ tathā sṛṣṭiṃ yadi dārḍhyena bhāvayet || SivSV_3.37:4 ||
body.translated_text: If one contemplates such arising creation with firmness, || SivSV_3.37:4 ||
Then there would be unlimited creation common to all || SivSV_3.37:5 ||
Since the power of creation here — the power having the nature of freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) — || SivSV_3.37:6 ||

body.text: * pramātur bodharūpasya sāraṃ tasmāt svamāyayā || SivSV_3.37:7 ||
body.translated_text: Is the essence of the knower whose nature is awareness; therefore, by one's own <s>māyā</s>, || SivSV_3.37:7 ||
For the stimulation of the power of freedom that has been concealed || SivSV_3.37:8 ||]
Vitalization beginning with the three phases (<s>tripadādy anuprāṇana</s>) // SivS_3.38 //

children.translated_text: The three phases — of waking, dreaming, and deep sleep, in sequence — || SivSV_3.38:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Each having the form of beginning, middle, and end, examined indirectly, || SivSV_3.38:2 ||
Consisting of the orientation toward the object, attachment to it, and unification with it, || SivSV_3.38:3 ||
Having the form of creation, maintenance, and dissolution — by <s>turya</s> (the fourth) itself, beginning with that, || SivSV_3.38:4 ||
Within those three, with the nature of dense bliss consisting of the aesthetic rapture (<s>camatkāra</s>) of wonder, || SivSV_3.38:5 ||
Even though concealed by <s>māyā</s> whose nature is obscuration, || SivSV_3.38:6 ||
Flashing for a moment like lightning in the enjoyment of various objects, || SivSV_3.38:7 ||
The practitioner should impart vitalization through attentiveness || SivSV_3.38:8 ||
By that very life of one's own self that has been vitalized, || SivSV_3.38:9 ||

body.text: * samyaguttejanaṃ kuryād yenāsau tanmayo bhavet || SivSV_3.38:10 ||
body.translated_text: One should fully stimulate so that one becomes one with that || SivSV_3.38:10 ||

body.text: * turyānuprāṇanaṃ proktaṃ jāgarādau purā triṣu || SivSV_3.38:11 ||
body.translated_text: The vitalization by <s>turya</s> in the three [states] beginning with waking was previously declared || SivSV_3.38:11 ||
By the <s>sūtra</s> 'the fourth...' and by this [<s>sūtra</s>] 'the three-phased...' etc.; || SivSV_3.38:12 ||
It is distinguished [here] as being in the junctures of beginning, middle, and end of waking etc. || SivSV_3.38:13 ||
Not only in the inward-turned state of one's true nature, || SivSV_3.38:14 ||

body.text: * tripadādiprāṇanam ity etad uktam athāpi tu || SivSV_3.38:15 ||]
body.translated_text: This vitalization beginning with the three phases has been stated; but furthermore || SivSV_3.38:15 ||]
As in the steady state of mind, so in body, senses, and external [objects] // SivS_3.39 //

children.text: * anuprāṇanam ity etad ādadyād iti śiṣyate || SivSV_3.39:1 ||
children.translated_text: This vitalization should be applied — so it is taught; || SivSV_3.39:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Just as in the inward-turned state of mind, so || SivSV_3.39:2 ||
With <s>turya</s> having the nature of bliss, which has been described as the vitalizer, || SivSV_3.39:3 ||
One should apply [it] even in the outward-turned [state] consisting of body, senses, and objects; || SivSV_3.39:4 ||

body.text: * tanmayaṃ bhavatīty arthāt tadā sarvaṃ carācaram || SivSV_3.39:5 ||
body.translated_text: Then everything, moving and unmoving, becomes permeated by that — this is the meaning || SivSV_3.39:5 ||
Thus, for one whose nature is his own bliss, the power characterized by freedom (<s>svātantrya</s>) || SivSV_3.39:6 ||
Clearly becomes the creator of desired objects || SivSV_3.39:7 ||

body.text: * yadā punar asau yogī proktāṃ turyātmikāṃ daśām || SivSV_3.39:8 ||
body.translated_text: But when this <s>yogin</s> [does not realize] the described state consisting of <s>turya</s>, || SivSV_3.39:8 ||

body.text: * āntarīṃ nāmṛśaty antas tadā dehādyahaṃkṛteḥ || SivSV_3.39:9 ||
body.translated_text: And does not inwardly contemplate the inner [awareness], then, due to the ego-identification with body etc., || SivSV_3.39:9 ||
Having the form of the feeling of incompleteness, of the nature of <s>āṇavamala</s> (primal impurity) || SivSV_3.39:10 ||]
Through desire, the outward movement of the one who is carried along (<s>saṃvāhya</s>) // SivS_3.40 //

children.translated_text: By the <s>tattvas</s> seized by the host of powers, ending with earth, beginning with <s>kalā</s>, || SivSV_3.40:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * yoner yonyantaraṃ neyaḥ saṃvāhyaḥ paśur ucyate || SivSV_3.40:2 ||
body.translated_text: The one who is led from one womb to another womb, the one carried along, is called a bound soul (<s>paśu</s>); || SivSV_3.40:2 ||
Of that [bound soul], having the form of <s>āṇavamala</s>, following various <s>karmas</s>, || SivSV_3.40:3 ||
From desire having the form of the feeling of incompleteness, there is outward movement; || SivSV_3.40:4 ||
Turning toward objects alone is his [nature], not the inward contemplation of the truth || SivSV_3.40:5 ||
But when, through the opening [of awareness] impelled by the descent of the power of the great Lord (<s>Maheśāna</s>), || SivSV_3.40:6 ||

body.text: * ātmīyam eva vimṛśan nāste rūpaṃ tadāsya tu || SivSV_3.40:7 ||
body.translated_text: Contemplating one's own nature alone, that [outward] form does not remain for him; || SivSV_3.40:7 ||

body.text: * abhāvād abhilāṣasya na bahirgatir āpatet || SivSV_3.40:8 ||
body.translated_text: Due to the absence of desire, outward movement would not occur || SivSV_3.40:8 ||
But rather, the state of one who delights in the Self while moving about as described — so it is said || SivSV_3.40:9 ||]
For one whose awareness has ascended to that, through the diminishing of that [desire], there is the diminishing of the individual soul (<s>jīva</s>) // SivS_3.41 //

children.translated_text: "That" — in the described realm of activity, whose nature is the state of being the knower, || SivSV_3.41:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
The awareness (<s>pramiti</s>) that has ascended, the consciousness devoted to reflecting on that, || SivSV_3.41:2 ||

body.text: * yasya tasyāsya tad iti proktāṇavamalātmanaḥ || SivSV_3.41:3 ||
body.translated_text: Of that one who has this — of that which is described as having the nature of <s>āṇavamala</s>, || SivSV_3.41:3 ||

body.text: * abhilāpasya rūḍhasya kṣayāj jīvasya saṃkṣayaḥ || SivSV_3.41:4 ||
body.translated_text: Through the diminishing of the established desire, there is the diminishing of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul); || SivSV_3.41:4 ||
The pacification of [that which has] the nature of the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) truly occurs || SivSV_3.41:5 ||

body.text: * prāpnoti dehapāto 'sya nanv evaṃ jīvasaṃkṣaye || SivSV_3.41:6 ||
body.translated_text: Does not the fall of the body occur for him? — surely, in the diminishing of the <s>jīva</s>, || SivSV_3.41:6 ||

body.text: * nāsau kadāpi kasyāpi dṛśyate 'trāpi yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.41:7 ||
body.translated_text: [Such a state] is never seen for anyone, even for the <s>yogin</s> here; || SivSV_3.41:7 ||

body.text: * tasmāt kathaṃ tadārūḍhapramitiḥ sādhako bhavet || SivSV_3.41:8 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore, how can the practitioner have awareness ascended to that? || SivSV_3.41:8 ||

body.text: * ity āśaṅkyottaraṃ vakti bhagavān viśvadaiśikaḥ || SivSV_3.41:9 ||]
body.translated_text: Anticipating this [doubt], the blessed universal teacher gives the answer || SivSV_3.41:9 ||]

body.text: bhūtakañcukī tadā vimukto bhūyaḥ patisamaḥ paraḥ // SivS_3.42 //
body.translated_text: Wearing the elements as a cloak, then liberated, again equal to the Lord (<s>pati</s>), supreme // SivS_3.42 //

children.translated_text: Upon the pacification of the described desire, in the diminishing of the <s>jīva</s>, || SivSV_3.42:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Even upon the dissolution of the identification with the subtle body (<s>puryaṣṭaka</s>) as the subject, || SivSV_3.42:2 ||
By the elements that cause the inception of the body, not touching the state of I-consciousness, || SivSV_3.42:3 ||
Like one wearing a cloak — especially liberated due to the fortune of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation); || SivSV_3.42:4 ||

body.text: * bhūyo bāhulyataḥ patyā samo 'yaṃ parameśinā || SivSV_3.42:5 ||
body.translated_text: Again, abundantly, this one is equal to the Lord, to <s>Parameśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord); || SivSV_3.42:5 ||
Having a nature dense with consciousness and bliss, absorbed in that [Lord's] essential nature; || SivSV_3.42:6 ||

body.text: * tata eva paraḥ pūrṇaḥ samyak tanmayatāṃ gataḥ || SivSV_3.42:7 ||
body.translated_text: From that very [realization], supreme, complete, having fully attained oneness with that || SivSV_3.42:7 ||

body.text: * bhūtakañcukitāpy asya tadaiva na nivartate || SivSV_3.42:8 ||
body.translated_text: Even the state of wearing the elements as a cloak does not then cease for him; || SivSV_3.42:8 ||

body.text: * kasmād ity api śaṅkāyām uttaraṃ vakti śaṃkaraḥ || SivSV_3.42:9 ||]
body.translated_text: To the doubt 'Why [not]?', <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) gives the answer || SivSV_3.42:9 ||]
The connection with <s>prāṇa</s> is natural // SivS_3.43 //

children.text: * prāṇe pariṇatā saṃvit prāg iti proktayā diśā || SivSV_3.43:1 ||
children.translated_text: Consciousness transformed into <s>prāṇa</s> — by the direction previously stated, || SivSV_3.43:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]

body.text: * nisargāt sahajāt svasya svātantryād anivāritāt || SivSV_3.43:2 ||
body.translated_text: From nature, from the innate, from one's own uninhibited freedom, || SivSV_3.43:2 ||
Through the desire to produce the excellence of the diversity of the moving manifold, || SivSV_3.43:3 ||

body.text: * saṃkocaṃ parigṛhṇānā saṃvid bhagavatī svayam || SivSV_3.43:4 ||
body.translated_text: The blessed consciousness (<s>saṃvid bhagavatī</s>) herself, taking on contraction, || SivSV_3.43:4 ||
Attains the contracting stages of being various <s>prāṇa</s>-experiencers || SivSV_3.43:5 ||

body.text: * uktam arthaṃ dṛḍhīkartuṃ saṃvādaḥ so 'yam atra tu || SivSV_3.43:6 ||
body.translated_text: To strengthen the stated meaning, here is this corroboration: || SivSV_3.43:6 ||

body.text: * yā sā śaktiḥ parā sūkṣmā vyāpinī nirmalā śivā || SivSV_3.43:7 ||
body.translated_text: That power which is supreme, subtle, pervading, pure, auspicious (<s>śivā</s>), || SivSV_3.43:7 ||
The mother of the circle of powers (<s>śakticakra</s>), having the nature of supreme blissful nectar, || SivSV_3.43:8 ||
The great <s>Ghoreśvarī</s>, fierce, the cause of creation and dissolution, || SivSV_3.43:9 ||

body.text: * trivahaṃ trividhaṃ triṣṭhaṃ balāt kālaṃ prakarṣati || SivSV_3.43:10 ||
body.translated_text: Forcefully draws time, which has three streams, is threefold, and abides in three || SivSV_3.43:10 ||

body.text: * iti vājasaneyāyām iyam eva citiḥ parā || SivSV_3.43:11 ||
body.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Vājasaneyī</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] — this indeed is the supreme consciousness; || SivSV_3.43:11 ||
Having descended by its own freedom previously into the knower in the form of <s>prāṇa</s>, || SivSV_3.43:12 ||
Flowing through the triad of channels whose nature is moon, sun, and fire, || SivSV_3.43:13 ||
Characterized by inhalation and exhalation, entering within and going out, || SivSV_3.43:14 ||
The threefold time — past, present, etc. — within oneself, || SivSV_3.43:15 ||

body.text: * karṣanty antar bahiś ceti kathyate kālakarṣiṇī || SivSV_3.43:16 ||
body.translated_text: Drawing inward and outward — thus she is called <s>kālakarṣiṇī</s> (the drawer of time) || SivSV_3.43:16 ||

body.text: * tato naisargikas tasyāḥ prāṇasambandha āgataḥ || SivSV_3.43:17 ||
body.translated_text: Therefore the natural connection of that [consciousness] with <s>prāṇa</s> has come about; || SivSV_3.43:17 ||

body.text: * sthite 'pi prāṇasambandhe yas tadārūḍha āntarīm || SivSV_3.43:18 ||
body.translated_text: Even while the connection with <s>prāṇa</s> remains, one who has ascended to that [state], the inner || SivSV_3.43:18 ||

body.text: * saṃvidaṃ vimṛśann āste sa lokottaratāṃ vrajet || SivSV_3.43:19 ||
body.translated_text: [One who] abides contemplating [inner] awareness, he would attain transcendence || SivSV_3.43:19 ||
Thus <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord) speaks by way of summarizing the means || SivSV_3.43:20 ||]
Through control at the center within the nostrils — what more [need be said] here regarding the left, right, and <s>suṣumnā</s> [channels]? // SivS_3.44 //

children.translated_text: Of the closely packed channels from the eyes to the pores of the hair, || SivSV_3.44:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Of all those [channels], in the principal ones that give support to all, || SivSV_3.44:2 ||
In the channel-paths of the left (<s>iḍā</s>), right (<s>piṅgalā</s>), and <s>suṣumnā</s>, always, || SivSV_3.44:3 ||
The nostril is the <s>prāṇaśakti</s> (vital power) of the channels, flowing in a curved path; || SivSV_3.44:4 ||

body.text: * antar ity āntarī saṃvit tatsvarūpasya yat punaḥ || SivSV_3.44:5 ||
body.translated_text: "Inner" means the inner consciousness; moreover, of its essential nature, || SivSV_3.44:5 ||
The center, being the innermost of all, is the principal [point], the canvas of the universe; || SivSV_3.44:6 ||

body.text: * parāmarśamayaṃ rūpam uttīrṇaṃ tasya saṃyamāt || SivSV_3.44:7 ||
body.translated_text: The form consisting of awareness, transcendent — through the control of that, || SivSV_3.44:7 ||
Arising from the excellence of contemplation, from the reflective awareness of self-knowledge, || SivSV_3.44:8 ||

body.text: * kim atra saṃyame vācyam iyam eva samāhitiḥ || SivSV_3.44:9 ||
body.translated_text: What need be said here about control? This itself is the state of <s>samādhi</s> (absorption); || SivSV_3.44:9 ||
Blazing within all states continuously, || SivSV_3.44:10 ||
It is experienced by the <s>yogin</s> alone through uninterrupted attentiveness || SivSV_3.44:11 ||

body.text: * mayy āveśya mano ye māṃ nityayuktā upāsate || SivSV_3.44:12 ||
body.translated_text: "Those who, fixing their mind on Me, worship Me, ever united [with Me], || SivSV_3.44:12 ||

body.text: * śraddhayā parayopetās te me yuktatamā matāḥ || SivSV_3.44:13 ||
body.translated_text: Endowed with supreme faith — they are considered by Me to be the most devoted" || SivSV_3.44:13 ||
Thus, following the principle declared in the blessed <s>Bhagavadgītā</s>, || SivSV_3.44:14 ||
For one whose mind is absorbed in the I-consciousness that transcends the universe, || SivSV_3.44:15 ||

body.text: * paryante yogino yogaphalaṃ samyak pradarśayan || SivSV_3.44:16 ||
body.translated_text: At the conclusion, fully demonstrating the fruit of yoga for the <s>yogin</s>, || SivSV_3.44:16 ||

body.text: * upasaṃharati śrīmān uktaṃ prakaraṇaṃ śivaḥ || SivSV_3.44:17 ||]
body.translated_text: The glorious <s>Śiva</s> brings to a close the stated treatise || SivSV_3.44:17 ||]
There would again be the closing of the eyes (<s>pratimīlana</s>) // SivS_3.45 //

children.translated_text: And again, having the nature of the opening of the described consciousness-nature, || SivSV_3.45:1 ||

body.translated_text: * [<s>Śivasūtravārttika</s>:]
Would occur for the supreme <s>yogin</s> who has ascended to the highest yoga; || SivSV_3.45:2 ||

body.text: * bhūyaḥ syād iti vākyasya sphuṭam evāyam āśayaḥ || SivSV_3.45:3 ||
body.translated_text: "There would be again" — this is clearly the meaning of the statement; || SivSV_3.45:3 ||

body.text: * yac chivatvam amuṣyoktaṃ nāpūrvaṃ tat tu yoginaḥ || SivSV_3.45:4 ||
body.translated_text: The <s>Śiva</s>-nature that has been described is not something new for the <s>yogin</s>; || SivSV_3.45:4 ||
It is his very own nature — those [obscurations] raised by the <s>māyā</s>-power from his own [self], || SivSV_3.45:5 ||

body.text: * nāyaṃ vikalpadaurātmyād bhāsamānam api svataḥ || SivSV_3.45:6 ||
body.translated_text: This [<s>yogin</s>], due to the wickedness of thought-constructs (<s>vikalpa</s>), though [his true nature is] shining of itself, || SivSV_3.45:6 ||

body.text: * vimraṣṭuṃ kṣama ity asya proktopāyakrameṇa tat || SivSV_3.45:7 ||
body.translated_text: Was not capable of reflecting [on it]; therefore through the described sequence of means, || SivSV_3.45:7 ||

body.text: * śivatvaṃ vyaktim etīti śivenodīritaṃ śivam || SivSV_3.45:8 ||
body.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s>-nature comes to manifestation — thus the auspicious [teaching] declared by <s>Śiva</s> || SivSV_3.45:8 ||
Thus this third opening (<s>unmeṣa</s>), indicating <s>āṇavopāya</s> (the individual means) || SivSV_3.45:9 ||
Thus, the <s>Śivasūtras</s>, enriched with secret meaning, || SivSV_3.45:10 ||
Together with the previously stated <s>vārttika</s> portion, [this is] another <s>vārttika</s>, || SivSV_3.45:11 ||
For those who are heirs to the sovereignty of undivided consciousness, || SivSV_3.45:12 ||
Whose wealth of thirty-six <s>tattvas</s> has been seized through the force of prowess, || SivSV_3.45:13 ||
For the sweet princes who ascend to the great I-consciousness, || SivSV_3.45:14 ||
By the last [birth], whose final birth is destroyed by that illumination, || SivSV_3.45:15 ||
By me, <s>Varadarāja</s>, dispelling the delusion of <s>māyā</s>, || SivSV_3.45:16 ||
Following the path of explanation determined by the glorious <s>Kṣemarāja</s>, || SivSV_3.45:17 ||
It has been elucidated simply and with compassion by the accomplished <s>Kṛṣṇadāsa</s>; || SivSV_3.45:18 ||

body.text: * anugṛhṇantu nāmaitat santaḥ saṃtoṣam āgatāḥ || SivSV_3.45:19 ||]
body.translated_text: May the saints, having attained satisfaction, bless this [work] || SivSV_3.45:19 ||]
